possessing residues of oblations and having recited over them, the giver, being caused to speak, should give them. / [63].29) With "This portion" (AV 6.122.1), "This, O companions" (AV 6.123.1), and "In the mortar" (AV 10.9.26), are the concluding offerings. / [63].30) He casts [grains] in. / [63].31) And the recitation of the consecration.

63.s: dvitīyaṃ tat pāpacailaṃ bhavati tan manuṣyāndhamāya dadyād ity eke
63.d: द्वितीयं तत् पापचैलं भवति तन् मनुष्यान्धमाय दद्याद् इत्य् एके

63.s: śṛtaṃ tvā havyam iti vatura ārṣeyān bhṛgvaṅgirovid upasādayati
63.d: शृतं त्वा हव्यम् इति वतुर आर्षेयान् भृग्वङ्गिरोविद् उपसादयति

63.s: pakvaṃ kṣetrāt varṣaṃ vanuṣva ity apakarṣati
63.d: पक्वं क्षेत्रात् वर्षं वनुष्व इत्य् अपकर्षति

63.s: paraḥ kambūkān iti savyena pādena phalīkaraṇān apohati
63.d: परः कम्बूकान् इति सव्येन पादेन फलीकरणान् अपोहति

63.s: agne prehi samācinuṣva ity ājyaṃ juhuyāt
63.d: अग्ने प्रेहि समाचिनुष्व इत्य् आज्यं जुहुयात्

63.s: liṅgaṃ parihitasya liṅgasyānantaraṃ karmakarmānupūrveṇa liṅgaṃ parīkṣeta
63.d: लिङ्गं परिहितस्य लिङ्गस्यानन्तरं कर्मकर्मानुपूर्वेण लिङ्गं परीक्षेत

63.s: śrāmyataḥ itiprabhṛtibhir vā sūktenābhimantryābhinigadya dadyād dātā vācyamānaḥ
63.d: श्राम्यतः इतिप्रभृतिभिर् वा सूक्तेनाभिमन्त्र्याभिनिगद्य दद्याद् दाता वाच्यमानः

63.s: prācyai tvā diśe itiprabhṛtibhir vānuvākenābhimantryābhinigadya dadyād dātā vācyamānaḥ
63.d: प्राच्यै त्वा दिशे इतिप्रभृतिभिर् वानुवाकेनाभिमन्त्र्याभिनिगद्य दद्याद् दाता वाच्यमानः

63.s: yathāsavam anyān pṛthag vā iti prakṛtiḥ
63.d: यथासवम् अन्यान् पृथग् वा इति प्रकृतिः

63.s: etaṃ bhāgaṃ etaṃ sadhasthāḥ ulūkhale iti saṃsthitahomāḥ
63.d: एतं भागं एतं सधस्थाः उलूखले इति संस्थितहोमाः

64.m:
[64].1) With: "Of the regions..." (AV 1.31.1), [he prepares] the four-platter offering.
[64].2) With: "What the kings..." (AV 3.29.1), he inspects [the goat].
[64].3) He places cakes separately on the feet of the one whose feet have been washed.
[64].4) A fifth [cake] on the navel.
[64].5) Tying [it] up with a garment, along with gold, endowed with the residue of oblations.
[64].6) With: "Bring this one near..." (AV 9.5.1), he addresses the goat being brought from the northeast.
[64].7) With: "A share for Indra..." (AV 9.5.2), [while it is] being led around the fire.
[64].8) With: "Those who hate us..." (AV 9.5.2c), [while it is] being quieted.
[64].9) With: "Forth the feet..." (AV 9.5.3), [while one is] washing the feet.
[64].10) With: "Having dissected with the dark [knife]..." (AV 9.5.4), [while one is] cutting it up joint by joint.
[64].11) With: "By a verse, the cooking pot..." (AV 9.5.5), [while one is] placing it on the fire.
[64].12) With: "Pour in..." (AV 9.5.5b), [while one is] pouring in [water].
[64].13) With: "Put down..." (AV 9.5.5b), [while one is] putting [the meat] in.
[64].14) With: "Place around..." (AV 9.5.5c), [while one is] placing [fuel] around.
[64].15) With: "Cooked, let it go..." (AV 9.5.5d), [while one is] removing it from the fire.
[64].16) With: "Step out from here..." (AV 9.5.6), [while one is] taking [the cooked meat] out upon darbha grass behind the fire.
[64].17) Having taken it out, with: "I anoint the goat..." (AV 4.14.6), he anoints it with ghee.
[64].18) With: "Endowed with five boiled messes of rice..." (AV 4.14.7), [the action is performed] as stated in the mantra.
[64].19) He places portions of boiled rice separately on the feet.
[64].20) A fifth in the middle.
[64].21) Having moistened the right hind-half with the sacrificial post,
[64].22) with: "The cooked goat..." (AV 4.14.9), [he lays out] the hide of this [goat] with the head and feet attached.
[64].23) With the hymn "For the goat..." (AV 4.14.1), [endowed] with the residue of oblations, as prescribed.
[64].24) In front of it he places an unwoven northern [cloth], together with gold.
[64].25) With: "Five golden ornaments..." (AV 9.5.25), [the action is performed] as stated in the mantra.
[64].26) To the north [he sets] a milch cow and other [gifts], a coverlet with a pillow, a garment, and gold,
[64].27) endowed with the residue of oblations by means of the hymn "Bring this one near..." (AV 9.5.1).
[64].28) Up to the anointing, the hundred-rice offering is explained by means of the five-rice offering.

64.s: ā nayaitam ity aparājitād ajamānīyamānam anumantrayate
64.d: आ नयैतम् इत्य् अपराजिताद् अजमानीयमानम् अनुमन्त्रयते

64.s: ut krāmātaḥ iti paścād agner darbheṣūddharantam
64.d: उत् क्रामातः इति पश्चाद् अग्नेर् दर्भेषूद्धरन्तम्

64.s: śṛtam ajaṃ ity anubaddhaśiraḥpādaṃ tu etasya carma
64.d: शृतम् अजं इत्य् अनुबद्धशिरःपादं तु एतस्य चर्म

64.s: ajo hi iti sūktena saṃpātavantaṃ yathoktam
64.d: अजो हि इति सूक्तेन संपातवन्तं यथोक्तम्

64.s: dhenvādīni uttarataḥ sopadhānam āstaraṇam vāso hiraṇyaṃ ca
64.d: धेन्वादीनि उत्तरतः सोपधानम् आस्तरणम् वासो हिरण्यं च

65.s: aghāyatām ity atra mukham apinahyamānam anumantrayate
65.d: अघायताम् इत्य् अत्र मुखम् अपिनह्यमानम् अनुमन्त्रयते
65.m: [65].1) With 'Of those who intend harm' [AV 10.9.1], he recites over its mouth as it is tied up here. / [65].2) With 'A thunderbolt against rivals' [AV 10.9.1b] and 'This press-stone indeed' [AV 10.9.2d], [he recites over it] as it falls down. / [65].3) With 'Thy altar' [AV 10.9.2], he spreads out what is specified in the mantra. / [65].4) In twenty pots of boiled oblation, they place upon the separate boiled oblations a hundred portions tied with leather thongs. / [65].5) In the first hollowed-out [part] of the middle one, [he places] curds; at the tenth, he encloses seven cakes on each side. / [65].6) At the fifteenth, two sacrificial cakes. / [65].7) At the front, gold. / [65].8) With 'The divine waters' [AV 10.9.27], [he places] water-jars in front. / [65].9) With the hymn 'Thy hair' [AV 10.9.3], [he renders] it endowed with the residue of oblations. / [65].10) Having led [the cow] clockwise around the fire, sitting down, washing, and sipping water are stated. / [65].11) Having brought water into his hand, / [65].12) then, having cut off twice from the middle and from the front part of that boiled oblation and portions, and having basted it with water from above, he offers [it into the fire] with: 'Purified by soma, sit in the belly of the Brahmans' [AV 11.1.25c] and 'I place thee, O boiled oblation, among the descendants of the ṛṣis' [AV 11.1.33a]. / [65].13) Then he eats. / [65].14) With: 'With the mouth of Agni I eat thee, with the mouth of Bṛhaspati; I place thee in the belly of Indra, in the stomach of Varuṇa; so, as he would eat what is offered and sacrificed, with the divine self I eat thee; thou art the self; hurt not my self in myself', he recites over what has been eaten. / [65].15) With: 'What Agni, named Nṛmaṇas, has entered into the brāhmaṇas; in him let this boiled oblation be well-offered for me; let him not harm me in the highest firmament; let it be for us in the highest firmament', he makes the giver recite. / [65].16) Up to the looking [upon the oblation], [the ritual] of the hundredfold boiled oblation is explained by the morning mutterings.

65.s: sapatneṣu vajram grāvā tvaiṣo iti nipatantam
65.d: सपत्नेषु वज्रम् ग्रावा त्वैषो इति निपतन्तम्

65.s: viṃśatyodanāsu śrayaṇīṣu śatam avadānāni vadhrīsaṃnaddhāni pṛthagodaneṣūpary ādadhati
65.d: विंशत्योदनासु श्रयणीषु शतम् अवदानानि वध्रीसंनद्धानि पृथगोदनेषूपर्य् आदधति

65.s: madhyamāyāḥ prathame randhriṇyāmikṣāṃ daśame abhitaḥ saptasaptāpūpān pariśrayati
65.d: मध्यमायाः प्रथमे रन्ध्रिण्यामिक्षां दशमे अभितः सप्तसप्तापूपान् परिश्रयति

65.s: athāmuṣya odanasyāvadānānāṃ ca madhyāt pūrvārdhāt ca dvir avadāya upariṣṭād udakenābhighārya juhoti somena pūto jaṭhare sīda brahmaṇām ārṣeyeṣu ni dadha odana tvā iti
65.d: अथामुष्य ओदनस्यावदानानां च मध्यात् पूर्वार्धात् च द्विर् अवदाय उपरिष्टाद् उदकेनाभिघार्य जुहोति सोमेन पूतो जठरे सीद ब्रह्मणाम् आर्षेयेषु नि दध ओदन त्वा इति

65.s: agneṣ ṭvāsyena prāśnāmi bṛhaspater mukhena | indrasya tvā jaṭhare sādayāmi varuṇasyodare | tad yathā hutam iṣṭaṃ prāśnīyād devātmā tvā prāśnāmy ātmāsy ātmann ātmānaṃ me mā hiṃsīr iti prāśitam anumantrayate
65.d: अग्नेष् ट्वास्येन प्राश्नामि बृहस्पतेर् मुखेन । इन्द्रस्य त्वा जठरे सादयामि वरुणस्योदरे । तद् यथा हुतम् इष्टं प्राश्नीयाद् देवात्मा त्वा प्राश्नाम्य् आत्मास्य् आत्मन्न् आत्मानं मे मा हिंसीर् इति प्राशितम् अनुमन्त्रयते

65.s: yo 'gnir nṛmaṇā nāma brāhmaṇeṣu praviṣṭaḥ | tasmin ma eṣa suhuto 'stv odanaḥ sa mā mā hiṃsīt parame vyoman || so asmabhyam astu parame vyomann iti dātāraṃ vācayati
65.d: यो ऽग्निर् नृमणा नाम ब्राह्मणेषु प्रविष्टः । तस्मिन् म एष सुहुतो ऽस्त्व् ओदनः स मा मा हिंसीत् परमे व्योमन् ॥ सो अस्मभ्यम् अस्तु परमे व्योमन्न् इति दातारं वाचयति

66.s: vāṅ ma āsan iti mantroktāni abhimantrayate
66.d: वाङ् म आसन् इति मन्त्रोक्तानि अभिमन्त्रयते
66.m: [66].1) With 'Speech in my mouth' [AV 19.60.1], he consecrates the [limbs] mentioned in the mantra. / [66].2) With 'Mind with the Bṛhat' [AV 5.10.8], 'And heaven to me' [AV 6.53.1], and 'May my vigor return to me' [AV 7.67.1], he recites in response. / [66].3) When it has been recited over in response, they divide it up and eat. / [66].4) In the hundredfold boiled oblation [rite], one hundred and twelve [cows are] the sacrificial fees. / [66].5) For one giving more, it turns out wish-fulfilling. / [66].6) With 'Brahman is its' [AV 4.34.1], he forms pools in the boiled oblation toward each cardinal direction. / [66].7) Above, a drinking vessel. / [66].8) Around it are four channels directed toward the cardinal points. / [66].9) He fills them with ritual fluids. / [66].10) Having placed upon the ground the things mentioned in the mantra containing liquor, water, lotus roots, and so on, toward each cardinal direction, / [66].11) with 'Which boiled oblation' [AV 4.35.1], [he gives the boiled oblation that overcomes] beyond death. / [66].12) With 'The draft ox' [AV 4.11.1], [he gives] a draft ox. / [66].13) With 'The rays of the sun' [AV 4.38.5], he gives a white cow with a barren cow [to follow]. / [66].14) With 'This dappled cow' [AV 6.31.1] and 'This thousand' [AV 7.22.1], [he gives] a dappled cow. / [66].15) With 'The gods this barley mingled with honey' [AV 6.30.1], [he gives] barley from Punahśilā containing honey, together with gold, and endowed with the residue of oblations. / [66].16) With 'May the divine people purify me' [AV 6.19.1], [he gives] a purifying dish of rice and pulse. / [66].17) With 'Who the dappled' [AV 7.104.1], [he gives] fertile land. / [66].18) With 'Pertaining to a thousand' [AV 9.4.1], [he gives] a bull. / [66].19) With 'And Prajāpati' [AV 9.7.1], [he gives] a draft ox. / [66].20) With 'Homage to thee being born' [AV 10.10.1] and 'I give' [AV 12.4.1], having besprinkled the barren cow with a water vessel endowed with the residue of oblations, having consecrated it, and having proclaimed [the formula], the giver, being made to speak, should give [it]. / [66].21) With 'The earth thee' [AV 3.29.8], he accepts her. / [66].22) With 'The upright post' [AV 9.3.1], whatever he is going to give together with the house is covered within it. / [66].23) But what is mentioned in the mantra is praised. / [66].24) With 'I unfasten of thy reed-mat' [AV 9.3.18], he pushes open the door. / [66].25) With 'Facing westward I approach thee facing westward' [AV 9.3.22], having taken the water vessel and the fire, they enter. / [66].26) Right within it, he makes it endowed with the residue of oblations with the hymn. / [66].27) Having besprinkled the house with the water vessel endowed with the residue of oblations, having consecrated it, and having proclaimed [the formula], the giver, being made to speak, should give [it]. / [66].28) With 'Between heaven and earth' [AV 9.3.15], he accepts it. / [66].29) With 'The upright post' [AV 9.3.1], he unbinds the [parts] mentioned in the mantra. / [66].30) Having consecrated it with 'Let not the bond on us' [AV 9.3.24], he holds it. / [66].31) With 'Not its bones' [AV 9.5.23], [he proceeds] as stated. / [66].32) With 'Gathering him up entirely' [AV 9.5.23c], having pierced [the ground], he pours [them] into a pit filled with water. / [66].33) And [he does likewise for] the hundredfold boiled oblation.

66.s: bṛhatā mano dyauś ca me punar maitv indriyaṃ iti pratimantrayate
66.d: बृहता मनो द्यौश् च मे पुनर् मैत्व् इन्द्रियं इति प्रतिमन्त्रयते

66.s: pratimantrite vyavadāyāśnanti
66.d: प्रतिमन्त्रिते व्यवदायाश्नन्ति

66.s: śataudanāyāṃ dvādaśaṃ śataṃ dakṣiṇāḥ
66.d: शतौदनायां द्वादशं शतं दक्षिणाः

66.s: adhikaṃ dadataḥ kāmapraṃ saṃpadyate
66.d: अधिकं ददतः कामप्रं संपद्यते

66.s: brahmāsya ity odane hradān pratidiśaṃ karoti
66.d: ब्रह्मास्य इत्य् ओदने ह्रदान् प्रतिदिशं करोति

66.s: upari āpānam
66.d: उपरि आपानम्

66.s: tadabhitaś catasro diśyāḥ kulyāḥ
66.d: तदभितश् चतस्रो दिश्याः कुल्याः

66.s: tā rasaiḥ pūrayati
66.d: ता रसैः पूरयति

66.s: pṛthivyāṃ surayādbhir āṇḍīkādivanti mantroktāni pratidiśaṃ nidhāya
66.d: पृथिव्यां सुरयाद्भिर् आण्डीकादिवन्ति मन्त्रोक्तानि प्रतिदिशं निधाय

66.s: yam odanaṃ ity atimṛtyum
66.d: यम् ओदनं इत्य् अतिमृत्युम्

66.s: anaḍvān ity anaḍvāham
66.d: अनड्वान् इत्य् अनड्वाहम्

66.s: sūryasya raśmīn iti karkīṃ sānūbandhyāṃ dadāti
66.d: सूर्यस्य रश्मीन् इति कर्कीं सानूबन्ध्यां ददाति

66.s: āyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnir ayaṃ sahasram iti pṛśnim gām
66.d: आयं गौः पृश्निर् अयं सहस्रम् इति पृश्निम् गाम्

66.s: devā imaṃ madunā saṃyutaṃ yavaṃ iti paunaḥśilaṃ madhumantaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ saṃpātavantam
66.d: देवा इमं मदुना संयुतं यवं इति पौनःशिलं मधुमन्तं सहिरण्यं संपातवन्तम्

66.s: punantu mā devajanāḥ iti pavitraṃ kṛśaram
66.d: पुनन्तु मा देवजनाः इति पवित्रं कृशरम्

66.s: kaḥ pṛśniṃ ity urvarām
66.d: कः पृश्निं इत्य् उर्वराम्

66.s: sāhasras ity ṛṣabham
66.d: साहस्रस् इत्य् ऋषभम्

66.s: prajāpatiś ca ity anaḍvāham
66.d: प्रजापतिश् च इत्य् अनड्वाहम्

66.s: namas te jāyamānāyai dadāmi iti vaśām udapātreṇa saṃpātavatā saṃprokṣyābhimantryābhinigadya dadyād dātā vācyamānaḥ
66.d: नमस् ते जायमानायै ददामि इति वशाम् उदपात्रेण संपातवता संप्रोक्ष्याभिमन्त्र्याभिनिगद्य दद्याद् दाता वाच्यमानः

66.s: bhūmiṣ ṭvā ity enāṃ pratigṛhṇāti
66.d: भूमिष् ट्वा इत्य् एनां प्रतिगृह्णाति

66.s: upamitāṃ iti yat śālayā saha dāsyan bhavati tad antar bhavati apihitam
66.d: उपमितां इति यत् शालया सह दास्यन् भवति तद् अन्तर् भवति अपिहितम्

66.s: mantroktaṃ tu praśastam
66.d: मन्त्रोक्तं तु प्रशस्तम्

66.s: iṭasya te vi cṛtāmi iti dvāram avasārayati
66.d: इटस्य ते वि चृतामि इति द्वारम् अवसारयति

66.s: pratīcīṃ tvā pratīcīnaḥ ity udapātram agnim ādāya prapadyante
66.d: प्रतीचीं त्वा प्रतीचीनः इत्य् उदपात्रम् अग्निम् आदाय प्रपद्यन्ते

66.s: tad antar eva sūktena saṃpātavat karoti
66.d: तद् अन्तर् एव सूक्तेन संपातवत् करोति

66.s: udapātreṇa saṃpātavatā śālāṃ saṃprokṣyābhimantryābhinigadya dadyād dātā vācyamānaḥ
66.d: उदपात्रेण संपातवता शालां संप्रोक्ष्याभिमन्त्र्याभिनिगद्य दद्याद् दाता वाच्यमानः

66.s: antarā dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca ity enāṃ pratigṛhṇāti
66.d: अन्तरा द्यां च पृथिवीं च इत्य् एनां प्रतिगृह्णाति

66.s: upamitāṃ iti mantroktāni pracṛtati
66.d: उपमितां इति मन्त्रोक्तानि प्रचृतति

66.s: mā naḥ pāśaṃ ity abhimantrya dhārayati
66.d: मा नः पाशं इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य धारयति

66.s: nāsyāsthīni iti yathoktam
66.d: नास्यास्थीनि इति यथोक्तम्

66.s: sarvam enaṃ samādaya ity adbhiḥ pūrṇe garte pravidhya saṃvapati
66.d: सर्वम् एनं समादय इत्य् अद्भिः पूर्णे गर्ते प्रविध्य संवपति

66.s: śataudanāṃ ca
66.d: शतौदनां च

67.s: saṃbhṛteṣu sāvikeṣu saṃbhāreṣu brāhmaṇam ṛtvijaṃ vṛṇīta
67.d: संभृतेषु साविकेषु संभारेषु ब्राह्मणम् ऋत्विजं वृणीत
67.m:
[67].1) When the ritual equipment for the sava offerings has been gathered, he should choose a Brahmin as sacrificial priest,
[67].2) a seer, born of seers, one whose sacrificial fee is readily given, and free from irregular occurrences.
[67].3) For he indeed is a seer, born of seers, one whose sacrificial fee is readily given, whose ancestors down to at least three generations are endowed with sacred learning, conduct, right behavior, and virtuous character.
[67].4) "During the northern course of the sun," say some.
[67].5) Now, therefore, we shall explain the ritual procedure for the cooked-rice savas.
[67].6) Having offered the savas, he should set up the sacred fires.
[67].7) "According to all the Vedas," say some.
[67].8) All the Vedas have two ritual options.
[67].9) The consecration lasts for at most a month, or twelve nights,
[67].10) "Three nights," say some.
[67].11) They should eat sacrificial food [and remain] celibate students.
[67].12) They should sleep on the ground.
[67].13) The officiant and the sacrificer should not eat according to desire until completion, if [the rites] are continuous.
[67].14) "It is concluded within a day," say some.
[67].15) For the sake of the undertaking, both givers, or the giver alone, should shave the hair of the head, beard, body hair, and nails.
[67].16) The wife [does the same], except for the hair of the head.
[67].17) Having bathed, wearing unwashed garments, fragrant, observing vows, and fit for the rite, they keep vigil.
[67].18) On the next day, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, having prepared pacifying water, and having thoroughly besprinkled the sacrificial ground, and having churned the fire for the Brahma-rice offering,
[67].19) while the giver touches him from behind, he should offer a full-spoon oblation with these three hymns: "Whatever offense against the gods, o gods" [6.114.1], "Whether knowing or unknowing" [6.115.1], and "What has been borrowed and not repaid" [6.117.1].
[67].20) In the forenoon, having arranged eastward the kindling wood of a pacified tree outside,
[67].21) having swept around, besprinkled around, strewn sacrificial grass around, set down the water vessel, and attended to the ghee with the serving vessel,
[67].22) having offered the regular preliminary oblations and the two ghee-portions,
[67].23) having strewn behind the fire an ox-hide or bull-hide—washed and prepared, or reddish—with its neck pointing east and hair uppermost,
[67].24) he prepares two strainers.
[67].25) Having washed two stalks of darbha grass whose tips are unbroken, he strokes them along the direction of the hair.
[67].26) Bending the right knee, facing the northeast, or bowing low, [he measures out the grain] with a fist, with an open hand, with joined palms, or with that [vessel] in which he is about to cook it, as a fourth option,
[67].27) with a saucer, a portion of four saucers, [saying]: "At the impulse of god Savitṛ...", "To the seers, to those born of seers, to you, the sole seer, I pour you out agreeable!"

67.s: eṣa ha vā ṛṣir ārṣeyaḥ sudhātudakṣiṇo yasya tryavarārdhyāḥ pūrvapuruṣā vidyācaraṇavṛttaśīlasaṃpannāḥ
67.d: एष ह वा ऋषिर् आर्षेयः सुधातुदक्षिणो यस्य त्र्यवरार्ध्याः पूर्वपुरुषा विद्याचरणवृत्तशीलसंपन्नाः

67.s: kartṛdātārau ā samāpanāt kāmaṃ na bhuñjīran saṃtatāś cet syuḥ
67.d: कर्तृदातारौ आ समापनात् कामं न भुञ्जीरन् संतताश् चेत् स्युः

67.s: yātrārthaṃ dātārau vā dātā keśaśmaśruromanakhāni vāpayīta
67.d: यात्रार्थं दातारौ वा दाता केशश्मश्रुरोमनखानि वापयीत

67.s: śvo bhūte yajñopavītī śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā yajñavāstu ca saṃprokṣya brahmaudanikam agniṃ mathitvā
67.d: श्वो भूते यज्ञोपवीती शान्त्युदकं कृत्वा यज्ञवास्तु च संप्रोक्ष्य ब्रह्मौदनिकम् अग्निं मथित्वा

67.s: yad devā devaheḍanaṃ yad vidvāṃso yad avidvāṃso 'pamityam apratīttaṃ ity etais tribhiḥ sūktair anvārabdhe dātari pūrṇahomaṃ juhuyāt
67.d: यद् देवा देवहेडनं यद् विद्वांसो यद् अविद्वांसो ऽपमित्यम् अप्रतीत्तं इत्य् एतैस् त्रिभिः सूक्तैर् अन्वारब्धे दातरि पूर्णहोमं जुहुयात्

67.s: pūrvāhṇe bāhyataḥ śāntavṛkṣasya idhmaṃ prāñcam upasamādhāya
67.d: पूर्वाह्णे बाह्यतः शान्तवृक्षस्य इध्मं प्राञ्चम् उपसमाधाय

67.s: parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya barhir udapātram upasādya paricaraṇenājyaṃ paricarya
67.d: परिसमुह्य पर्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य बर्हिर् उदपात्रम् उपसाद्य परिचरणेनाज्यं परिचर्य

67.s: paścād agneḥ palpūlitavihitam aukṣaṃ vānaḍuham vā rohitaṃ carma prāggrīvam uttaraloma paristīrya
67.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेः पल्पूलितविहितम् औक्षं वानडुहम् वा रोहितं चर्म प्राग्ग्रीवम् उत्तरलोम परिस्तीर्य

67.s: dakṣiṇaṃ jānu ācyāparājitābhimukhaḥ prahvo vā muṣṭinā prasṛtināñjalinā yasyāṃ śrapayiṣyan syāt tayā caturtham
67.d: दक्षिणं जानु आच्यापराजिताभिमुखः प्रह्वो वा मुष्टिना प्रसृतिनाञ्जलिना यस्यां श्रपयिष्यन् स्यात् तया चतुर्थम्

67.s: śarāveṇa catuḥśarāvaṃ devasya tvā savituḥ prasave ṛṣibhyas tvārṣeyebhyas tvaikarṣaye tvā juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi
67.d: शरावेण चतुःशरावं देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऋषिभ्यस् त्वार्षेयेभ्यस् त्वैकर्षये त्वा जुष्टं निर्वपामि

68.s: vasavas tvā gāyatreṇa chandasā nir vapantu | ūrjam akṣitam akṣīyamāṇam upajīvyāsam iti dātāraṃ vācayati
68.d: वसवस् त्वा गायत्रेण छन्दसा निर् वपन्तु । ऊर्जम् अक्षितम् अक्षीयमाणम् उपजीव्यासम् इति दातारं वाचयति
68.m:
[68].1) He makes the donor recite: 'May the Vasus pour you out with the gāyatrī metre! May I subsist on sap, unexhausted and inexhaustible.'
[68].2) He makes the donor recite: 'May the Rudras [pour you out] with the triṣṭubh metre! May the Ādityas [pour you out] with the jagatī metre! May the All-Gods pour you out with the anuṣṭubh metre! May I subsist on sap, unexhausted and inexhaustible.'
[68].3) With the hymn, he touches what has been poured out.
[68].4) The svargaudana and brahmaudana form the framework.
[68].5) At their confluence, he should pour in two parts of water, measured to the brahmaudana.
[68].6) As many as the grains of rice may be, he should not pour water over, nor should he pour water upon [the offering].
[68].7) If he should pour water over, the Brahman priest makes the sacrificer recite: 'Upon me be splendour and also renown…'
[68].8) Then he should pour water upon [it].
[68].9) He should pour water upon [it] with the two [stanzas]: 'Swell up…' and 'May your saps…'
[68].10) 'Swell up, may virile strength come together to you from all sides, O Soma; be [present] in the gathering of prize! / May your saps, may prizes unite, may virile powers unite, overcoming hostility; swelling up for immortality, O Soma, place the highest glories in heaven!'—thus.
[68].11) If at that point he should not touch salt even to the measure of a fingernail, on that account it becomes plain food for him.
[68].12) An unwashed garment lies to the south.
[68].13) That [is accompanied] with gold.
[68].14) There, two water vessels are placed.
[68].15) One is the southern one, the other is the inner one.
[68].16) The inner one is that from which he will perform the rite.
[68].17) The outer one belongs to Jāṅmāyana.
[68].18) Having taken water from that, he pours it into the pot.
[68].19) With a ladle into the cooking pot.
[68].20) When made [ready] by the ladle, he pours it back right there.
[68].21) Having taken the uppermost portion with the ladle, his friend, sitting to the south of the fire facing north, holds it.
[68].22) Then he dishes out [the boiled oblation].
[68].23) When it has been dished out, having placed in the northern half what he took and held, and having besprinkled it with ritual fluids, the donor brings it near to the recipient.
[68].24) While [the recipient] maintains contact with it, he makes the donor recite:
[68].25) The regular hymn foot by foot by one who has bathed: 'Which two wings of yours…', 'When you stood…'
[68].26) 'Which two unaging, feathered wings of yours, with which you strike away the demons, O boiled oblation, / with those two may we proceed along the path to the world of the virtuous, where the primeval, first-born seers are. / When you stood upon the back of heaven, above the vault, O boiled oblation, / the Brāhmaṇas whose law is truth followed along together with the gift.'
[68].27) 'Stride up to the firmament with the fire…', 'From the back of the earth I have mounted the atmosphere…', 'Going to the sun, they looked not back…', 'Extend wide with great greatness…', 'This light of mine…', 'And for truth…', thus three, together with this one: 'United the fires…'
[68].28) After this, when it has been recited, offered, and concluded, he should touch [it], uttering his name: 'I give you this one.'
[68].29) With the sacrificial fee, 'Desire in the beginning…'—as has been stated.
[68].30) 'They who, eating…' are the preparatory oblations.
[68].31) 'O Agni, be closest to us, and a protector, kindly, providing shelter. / To you, brightest, shining one, we now pray for favour, for our friends,' [and] 'Swell the household, slayer of sickness, finder of goods, increaser of prosperity, / be a good friend, be well-disposed'—these are the two portions of ghee.
[68].32) 'Having brought water in the hand'—as has been stated.
[68].33) Ending with the counter-mantra.
[68].34) When the counter-mantra has been recited, they divide [it] and eat.
[68].35) With 'To Idāvatsara…' he should offer ghee as the release from the vow.
[68].36) He should put on the firewood sticks.
[68].37) There are two verses on this: 'When fire is churned with a sacrificial formula, and set up with a sacrificial formula, / having given the Sava offerings, how can the dismissal of the Sava fire take place? / Having made him recite all the Savas, and having accepted them according to the rule, / and having offered with the Saṃnati formulas, Kauśika taught the dismissal there.'
[68].38) They go to the east or to the unvanquished direction (north-east) for the concluding bath.
[68].39) Having bathed with the water hymns, having turned clockwise, and having touched water without looking back, they return.
[68].40) They satisfy the Brāhmaṇas with food.
[68].41) Sacrificial fees are as stated, sacrificial fees are as stated.

68.s: rudrās tvā traiṣṭubhena chandasā | ādityās tvā jāgatena chandasā | viśve tvā devā ānuṣṭubhena chandasā nir vapantu | ūrjam akṣitam akṣīyamāṇam upa jīvyāsam iti dātāraṃ vācayati
68.d: रुद्रास् त्वा त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसा । आदित्यास् त्वा जागतेन छन्दसा । विश्वे त्वा देवा आनुष्टुभेन छन्दसा निर् वपन्तु । ऊर्जम् अक्षितम् अक्षीयमाणम् उप जीव्यासम् इति दातारं वाचयति

68.s: yāvantas taṇḍulāḥ syur nāvasiñcet na pratiṣiñcet
68.d: यावन्तस् तण्डुलाः स्युर् नावसिञ्चेत् न प्रतिषिञ्चेत्

68.s: yadi avasiñcet mayi varco atho yaśo iti brahmā yajamānaṃ vācayati
68.d: यदि अवसिञ्चेत् मयि वर्चो अथो यशो इति ब्रह्मा यजमानं वाचयति

68.s: ā pyāyasva saṃ te payāṃsi iti dvābhyāṃ pratiṣiñcet
68.d: आ प्यायस्व सं ते पयांसि इति द्वाभ्यां प्रतिषिञ्चेत्

68.s: ā pyāyasva sam etu te visvataḥ soma vṛṣṇyam | bhavā vājasya saṃgathe || saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājāḥ saṃ vṛṣṇyāny abhimātiṣāhaḥ | āpyāyamāno amṛtāya soma divi śravāṃsy uttamāni dhiṣva || iti
68.d: आ प्यायस्व सम् एतु ते विस्वतः सोम वृष्ण्यम् । भवा वाजस्य संगथे ॥ सं ते पयांसि सम् उ यन्तु वाजाः सं वृष्ण्यान्य् अभिमातिषाहः । आप्यायमानो अमृताय सोम दिवि श्रवांस्य् उत्तमानि धिष्व ॥ इति

68.s: tatra ced upādhimātrāyāṃ nakhena na lavaṇasya kuryāt tena evāsya tad vṛthānnaṃ saṃpadyate
68.d: तत्र चेद् उपाधिमात्रायां नखेन न लवणस्य कुर्यात् तेन एवास्य तद् वृथान्नं संपद्यते

68.s: darvyā uttamam apādāya tatsuhṛd dakṣiṇato agner udaṅmukha āsīno dhārayati
68.d: दर्व्या उत्तमम् अपादाय तत्सुहृद् दक्षिणतो अग्नेर् उदङ्मुख आसीनो धारयति

68.s: uddhṛte yad apādāya dhārayati tad uttarārdha ādhāya rasair upasicya pratigrahītre dātā upavahati
68.d: उद्धृते यद् अपादाय धारयति तद् उत्तरार्ध आधाय रसैर् उपसिच्य प्रतिग्रहीत्रे दाता उपवहति

68.s: tantraṃ sūktaṃ pacchaḥ snātena yau te pakṣau yad atiṣṭhaḥ
68.d: तन्त्रं सूक्तं पच्छः स्नातेन यौ ते पक्षौ यद् अतिष्ठः

68.s: yau te pakṣāv ajarau patatriṇau yābhyāṃ rakṣāṃsy apahaṃsy odana | tābhyāṃ pathyāsma sukṛtasya lokaṃ yatra ṛṣayaḥ prathamajāḥ purāṇāḥ || yad atiṣṭho divas pṛṣṭhe vyomann adhy odana | anvāyan satyadharmāṇo brāhmaṇā rādhasā saha |
68.d: यौ ते पक्षाव् अजरौ पतत्रिणौ याभ्यां रक्षांस्य् अपहंस्य् ओदन । ताभ्यां पथ्यास्म सुकृतस्य लोकं यत्र ऋषयः प्रथमजाः पुराणाः ॥ यद् अतिष्ठो दिवस् पृष्ठे व्योमन्न् अध्य् ओदन । अन्वायन् सत्यधर्माणो ब्राह्मणा राधसा सह ।

68.s: kramadhvam agninā nākam pṛṣṭhāt pṛthivyā aham antarikṣam āruham svar yanto nāpekṣanta uruḥ prathasva mahatā mahimnā idaṃ me jyotir satyāya ca iti tisraḥ sam agnayaḥ iti sārdham etayā
68.d: क्रमध्वम् अग्निना नाकम् पृष्ठात् पृथिव्या अहम् अन्तरिक्षम् आरुहम् स्वर् यन्तो नापेक्षन्त उरुः प्रथस्व महता महिम्ना इदं मे ज्योतिर् सत्याय च इति तिस्रः सम् अग्नयः इति सार्धम् एतया

68.s: ata ūrdhvaṃ vācite hute saṃsthite amūṃ te dadāmīti nāmagrāham upaspṛśet
68.d: अत ऊर्ध्वं वाचिते हुते संस्थिते अमूं ते ददामीति नामग्राहम् उपस्पृशेत्

68.s: agne tvaṃ no antama uta trātā śivo bhavā varūthyaḥ | taṃ tvā śociṣṭha dīdivaḥ sumnāya nūnam īmahe sakhibhyaḥ || gayasphāno amīvahā vasuvit puṣṭivardhanaḥ | sumitraḥ sumano bhava ity ājyabhāgau
68.d: अग्ने त्वं नो अन्तम उत त्राता शिवो भवा वरूथ्यः । तं त्वा शोचिष्ठ दीदिवः सुम्नाय नूनम् ईमहे सखिभ्यः ॥ गयस्फानो अमीवहा वसुवित् पुष्टिवर्धनः । सुमित्रः सुमनो भव इत्य् आज्यभागौ

68.s: tatra ślokau | yajuṣā mathite agnau yajuṣopasamāhite | savān dattvā savāgnes tu katham utsarjanaṃ bhavet || vācayitvā savān sarvān pratigṛhya yathāvidhi | hutvā saṃnatibhis tatrotsargaṃ kauśiko 'bravīt
68.d: तत्र श्लोकौ । यजुषा मथिते अग्नौ यजुषोपसमाहिते । सवान् दत्त्वा सवाग्नेस् तु कथम् उत्सर्जनं भवेत् ॥ वाचयित्वा सवान् सर्वान् प्रतिगृह्य यथाविधि । हुत्वा संनतिभिस् तत्रोत्सर्गं कौशिको ऽब्रवीत्

68.s: prāñco aparājitāṃ vā diśam avabhṛthāya vrajanti
68.d: प्राञ्चो अपराजितां वा दिशम् अवभृथाय व्रजन्ति

68.s: apāṃ sūktair āplutya pradakṣiṇam āvṛtyāpa upaspṛśyānavekṣamāṇāḥ pratyudāvrajanti
68.d: अपां सूक्तैर् आप्लुत्य प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्याप उपस्पृश्यानवेक्षमाणाः प्रत्युदाव्रजन्ति

69.s: pitryam agniṃ śamayiṣyañ jyeṣṭhasya cāvibhaktina ekāgnim ādhāsyan
69.d: पित्र्यम् अग्निं शमयिष्यञ् ज्येष्ठस्य चाविभक्तिन एकाग्निम् आधास्यन्
69.m:
[69].1) When about to extinguish the ancestral fire and about to establish a single fire for the eldest undivided brother,
[69].2) on the new moon day, in the eastern shed, he causes a two-year-old, red, uniformly colored cow to be tied up.
[69].3) At night, clad in a woolen shirt, the eldest touches [the fire or officiant] from behind.
[69].4) The wife, wearing an unwashed garment, [touches] the eldest from behind.
[69].5) The others [touch] the wife in succession behind.
[69].6) Then he causes them to pronounce: "O Adhrigu, pacify! Thoroughly pacifying, pacify! Pacify, o Adhrigu!" three times.
[69].7) With the verse "This Agni is the lord of the true" [7.62.1], the lesson "Mount the reed" [12.2.1], and the great pacification formula, he scatters [ingredients] into the pacifying water.
[69].8) With "O Agni, who does not consume corpses" [12.2.42], he holds a lamp [taken] from the frying-pan/fire-pan.
[69].9) And having dug up the scorched [earth] from the ground,
[69].10) having strewn it with clods of earth from an anthill,
[69].11) having smeared it over with a ball of dung,
[69].12) having scattered sand and sprinkled water over it,
[69].13) having made the ritual line,
[69].14) having sprinkled it again with water,
[69].15) having placed the churning-sticks to the west of the ritual line,
[69].16) having strewn them with the hairs of male cattle, horses, goats, and sheep, and with grains of rice and barley, and having wiped them with a ball of dung, he sets down two eastward-pointing stalks of darbha grass.
[69].17) With "You two are the two testicles" he takes the two churning-sticks into his hands,
[69].18) upon them the lower churning-stick,
[69].19) with the root-ends to the south,
[69].20) with the birth-cleft to the west, with "You are Urvaśī" and "You are Āyu";
[69].21) having joined the upper churning-stick from the root,
[69].22) having invoked [Agni] with "The conqueror of armies" [7.63.1],
[69].23) turning clockwise, the eldest churns three times [saying]: "Oṃ bhūr, be born according to the Gāyatrī meter, the Triṣṭubh, the Jagatī, the Anuṣṭubh meter! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar, begetter, om!"
[69].24) From this point onward, according to desire.

69.s: amāvāsyāyaṃ pūrvasminn upaśāle gāṃ dvihāyanīṃ rohiṇīm ekarūpāṃ bandhayati
69.d: अमावास्यायं पूर्वस्मिन्न् उपशाले गां द्विहायनीं रोहिणीम् एकरूपां बन्धयति

69.s: atha enān abhivyāhārayati adhrigo śamīdhvam | suśami śamīdhvam | śamīdhvam adhrigā o u iti triḥ
69.d: अथ एनान् अभिव्याहारयति अध्रिगो शमीध्वम् । सुशमि शमीध्वम् । शमीध्वम् अध्रिगा ओ उ इति त्रिः

69.s: ayam agniḥ satpatir naḍam ā roha ity anuvākaṃ mahāśāntiṃ ca śāntyudaka āvapate
69.d: अयम् अग्निः सत्पतिर् नडम् आ रोह इत्य् अनुवाकं महाशान्तिं च शान्त्युदक आवपते

69.s: agne akravyād iti bhraṣṭād dīpaṃ dhārayati
69.d: अग्ने अक्रव्याद् इति भ्रष्टाद् दीपं धारयति

69.s: go'śvājāvīnāṃ puṃsāṃ lomabhir āstīrya vrīhiyavaiś ca śakṛtpiṇḍam abhivimṛjya prāñcau darbhau nidadhāti
69.d: गोऽश्वाजावीनां पुंसां लोमभिर् आस्तीर्य व्रीहियवैश् च शकृत्पिण्डम् अभिविमृज्य प्राञ्चौ दर्भौ निदधाति

69.s: paścāt prajananām urvaśy asi ity āyur asi iti
69.d: पश्चात् प्रजननाम् उर्वश्य् असि इत्य् आयुर् असि इति

69.s: abhidakṣiṇaṃ jyeṣṭhas trir abhimanthati oṃ bhūr gāyatraṃ chando 'nuprajāyasva traiṣṭhubhaṃ jāgatam ānuṣṭhubam oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om iti
69.d: अभिदक्षिणं ज्येष्ठस् त्रिर् अभिमन्थति ओं भूर् गायत्रं छन्दो ऽनुप्रजायस्व त्रैष्ठुभं जागतम् आनुष्ठुबम् ओं भूर् भुवः स्वर् जनद् ओम् इति

70.s: manthāmi tvā jātavedaḥ sujātaṃ jātavedasam | sa no jīveṣv ā bhaja dīrgham āyuś ca dhehi naḥ || jāto 'janiṣṭhā yaśasā sahāgre prajāṃ paśūṃs tejo rayim asmāsu dhehi | ānandino modamānāḥ suvīrā anāmayāḥ sarvam āyur gamema || ud dīpyasva jātavedo 'va sediṃ tṛṇāṃ kṣudhaṃ jahi | apāsmat tama uchatv apa hrītamukho jahy apa durhārddiśo jahi || ihaivaidhi dhanasanir iha tvā sam idhīmahi | ihaidhi puṣṭivardhana iha tvā sam idhīmahi iti
70.d: मन्थामि त्वा जातवेदः सुजातं जातवेदसम् । स नो जीवेष्व् आ भज दीर्घम् आयुश् च धेहि नः ॥ जातो ऽजनिष्ठा यशसा सहाग्रे प्रजां पशूंस् तेजो रयिम् अस्मासु धेहि । आनन्दिनो मोदमानाः सुवीरा अनामयाः सर्वम् आयुर् गमेम ॥ उद् दीप्यस्व जातवेदो ऽव सेदिं तृणां क्षुधं जहि । अपास्मत् तम उछत्व् अप ह्रीतमुखो जह्य् अप दुर्हार्द्दिशो जहि ॥ इहैवैधि धनसनिर् इह त्वा सम् इधीमहि । इहैधि पुष्टिवर्धन इह त्वा सम् इधीमहि इति

70.s: yat tvā kruddhāḥ iti ca oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om ity aṅgirasāṃ tvā devānām ādityānāṃ vratenā dadhe | dyaur mahnāsi bhūmir bhūmnā tasyās te devy aditir upasthe 'nnādāyānnapatyāyā dadhat iti
70.d: यत् त्वा क्रुद्धाः इति च ओं भूर् भुवः स्वर् जनद् ओम् इत्य् अङ्गिरसां त्वा देवानाम् आदित्यानां व्रतेना दधे । द्यौर् मह्नासि भूमिर् भूम्ना तस्यास् ते देव्य् अदितिर् उपस्थे ऽन्नादायान्नपत्याया दधत् इति

70.s: agne gṛhapate sugṛhapatir ahaṃ tvayāgne gṛhapatinā bhūyāsam | sugṛhapatis tvaṃ mayāgne gṛhapatinā bhūyāḥ | asthūri ṇau gārhapatyāni dīdihi śataṃ samāḥ iti
70.d: अग्ने गृहपते सुगृहपतिर् अहं त्वयाग्ने गृहपतिना भूयासम् । सुगृहपतिस् त्वं मयाग्ने गृहपतिना भूयाः । अस्थूरि णौ गार्हपत्यानि दीदिहि शतं समाः इति

70.s: yo no agniḥ iti saha kartrā hṛdayāni abhimṛśante
70.d: यो नो अग्निः इति सह कर्त्रा हृदयानि अभिमृशन्ते

71.s: aṃśo rājā vibhajatīmāv agnī vidhārayan | kravyādaṃ nir ṇudāmasi havyavāḍ iha tiṣṭhatu iti vibhāgaṃ japati
71.d: अंशो राजा विभजतीमाव् अग्नी विधारयन् । क्रव्यादं निर् णुदामसि हव्यवाड् इह तिष्ठतु इति विभागं जपति
71.m:
[71].1) With the verse, 'King Aṃśa divides, keeping these two fires apart; we drive away the flesh-eating [fire], let the bearer of oblations remain here', he mutters the division.
[71].2) With the mantra 'Bringing good household fires' [AV 12.2.45c], he places a firewood stick upon the Gārhapatya fire with his right hand.
[71].3) With the mantra 'The flesh-eating one that was, that I have pacified' [cf. AV 3.21.9], he places a reed stick upon the flesh-eating fire with his left hand.
[71].4) Having placed outside what is prescribed in the mantra with 'Having turned away' [AV 12.2.34],
[71].5) he adds kindling with 'Mount the reed' [AV 12.2.1], 'They kindle' [AV 12.1.11], 'The old reed-stalk' [AV 12.1.54], and 'The backward sun' [AV 12.1.55].
[71].6) With 'If fire...' [AV 12.2.4], 'The fire that...' [AV 12.2.7], 'A black sheep...' [AV 12.2.53], and 'Do not roar at us, O blazing one; may Bharata be gracious and favorable to us; the fierce piercer has seized [it]; I pacify all the flesh-eating fires', he offers bean-flour with an oyster-shell.
[71].7) Placing lead in a wooden ladle and tying it up, offering a stir-drink, he should pacify it.
[71].8) With four verses beginning with 'Mount the reed' [AV 12.2.1], and with 'O non-flesh-eating Agni' [AV 12.2.42], 'This flesh-eating one' [AV 12.2.43], 'That which is in our horses' [AV 12.2.15], 'Thee to others' [AV 12.2.16], and 'The golden-handed' [AV 3.21.8], he pacifies [the fire].
[71].9) To the south, he carries the cool ashes over into an old store-room.
[71].10) Having made it thoroughly pacified with pacifying water, and having dug out the burnt earth,
[71].11) he makes [the elder brother] rise with 'Go far away, O Death' [AV 12.2.21].
[71].12) With the three verses beginning with 'The flesh-eating one' [AV 12.2.8], he recites over it while it is being carried away.
[71].13) From the lamp onwards up to the recitation, it has been explained by the carrying-back [ritual].
[71].14) With 'A black sheep' [AV 12.2.53], he deposits [it].
[71].15) [He deposits] pieces of lead into the cupped hands of the eldest brother, excluding the last one.
[71].16) He makes them wash off into [the lead] with 'In this we...' [AV 12.2.13], 'Whatever defilement...' [AV 12.2.40], and 'Wipe off onto the lead' [AV 12.2.19].
[71].17) Having wiped their hands and feet with black wool,
[71].18) [he performs] what is prescribed by the mantra with 'These living ones' [AV 12.2.22] and 'By the northward ones' [AV 12.2.29].
[71].19) Having effaced the footprints with a twig of the kūdī tree towards the rivers with 'Thrice seven' [AV 12.2.29c],
[71].20) and the boats with the second [verse, namely] 'The footprint of Death' [AV 12.2.30],
[71].21) having flung the kūdī twig towards the southeast with 'Go far away, O Death' [AV 12.2.21],
[71].22) having caused seven mock rivers to be made and filled with water,
[71].23) he makes them board a boat containing gold and barley with 'Board this boat of Savitṛ' [AV 12.2.48c], 'Providing good protection' [AV 7.6.3], and 'The great [earth] indeed' [AV 7.6.2].
[71].24) With 'The stony [river] flows' [AV 12.2.26] and 'Rise up, cross over, O companions' [AV 12.2.27], he makes them cross over toward the north.

71.s: sugārhapatyo iti dakṣiṇena gārhapatye samidham ādadhāti
71.d: सुगार्हपत्यो इति दक्षिणेन गार्हपत्ये समिधम् आदधाति

71.s: yaḥ kravyāt tam aśīśamam iti savyena naḍamayīṃ kravyādi
71.d: यः क्रव्यात् तम् अशीशमम् इति सव्येन नडमयीं क्रव्यादि

71.s: apāvṛtya iti mantroktaṃ bāhyato nidhāya
71.d: अपावृत्य इति मन्त्रोक्तं बाह्यतो निधाय

71.s: naḍam ā roha sam indhate iṣīkāṃ jaratīm pratyañcam arkaṃ ity upasamādadhāti
71.d: नडम् आ रोह सम् इन्धते इषीकां जरतीम् प्रत्यञ्चम् अर्कं इत्य् उपसमादधाति

71.s: yady agniḥ yo agniḥ aviḥ kṛṣṇā mā no ruroḥ śucadvidaḥ śivo no astu bharato rarāṇaḥ | ativyādhī vyādho agrabhīṣṭa kravyādo agnīñ śamayāmi sarvān iti śuktyā māṣapiṣṭāni juhoti
71.d: यद्य् अग्निः यो अग्निः अविः कृष्णा मा नो रुरोः शुचद्विदः शिवो नो अस्तु भरतो रराणः । अतिव्याधी व्याधो अग्रभीष्ट क्रव्यादो अग्नीञ् शमयामि सर्वान् इति शुक्त्या माषपिष्टानि जुहोति

71.s: sīsaṃ darvyām avadhāya udgrathya manthaṃ juhvan śamayet
71.d: सीसं दर्व्याम् अवधाय उद्ग्रथ्य मन्थं जुह्वन् शमयेत्

71.s: naḍam ā roha iti catasro agne akravyād imaṃ kravyād yo no aśveṣu anyebhyas tvā hiraṇyapāṇiṃ iti śamayati
71.d: नडम् आ रोह इति चतस्रो अग्ने अक्रव्याद् इमं क्रव्याद् यो नो अश्वेषु अन्येभ्यस् त्वा हिरण्यपाणिं इति शमयति

71.s: dakṣiṇato jaratkoṣṭhe śītaṃ bhasmābhiviharati
71.d: दक्षिणतो जरत्कोष्ठे शीतं भस्माभिविहरति

71.s: śāntyudakena suśāntaṃ kṛtvāvadagdhaṃ samutkhāya
71.d: शान्त्युदकेन सुशान्तं कृत्वावदग्धं समुत्खाय

71.s: paraṃ mṛtyo ity utthāpayati
71.d: परं मृत्यो इत्य् उत्थापयति

71.s: kravyādam iti tisṛbhir hrīyamāṇam anumantrayate
71.d: क्रव्यादम् इति तिसृभिर् ह्रीयमाणम् अनुमन्त्रयते

71.s: dīpādi ābhinigadanāt pratiharaṇena vyākhyātam
71.d: दीपादि आभिनिगदनात् प्रतिहरणेन व्याख्यातम्

71.s: aviḥ kṛṣṇā iti nidadhāti
71.d: अविः कृष्णा इति निदधाति

71.s: uttamavarjaṃ jyeṣṭhasyāñjalau sīsāni
71.d: उत्तमवर्जं ज्येष्ठस्याञ्जलौ सीसानि

71.s: asmin vayaṃ yad ripraṃ sīse mṛḍḍhvaṃ ity abhyavanejayati
71.d: अस्मिन् वयं यद् रिप्रं सीसे मृड्ढ्वं इत्य् अभ्यवनेजयति

71.s: kṛṣṇorṇayā pāṇipādān nimṛjya
71.d: कृष्णोर्णया पाणिपादान् निमृज्य

71.s: ime jīvā udīcīnaiḥ iti mantroktam
71.d: इमे जीवा उदीचीनैः इति मन्त्रोक्तम्

71.s: triḥ sapta iti kūdyā padāni lopayitvā nadībhyaḥ
71.d: त्रिः सप्त इति कूद्या पदानि लोपयित्वा नदीभ्यः

71.s: mṛtyoḥ padaṃ iti dvitīyayā nāvaḥ
71.d: मृत्योः पदं इति द्वितीयया नावः

71.s: paraṃ mṛtyo iti prāgdakṣiṇam kūdīṃ pravidhya
71.d: परं मृत्यो इति प्राग्दक्षिणम् कूदीं प्रविध्य

71.s: sapta nadīrūpāṇi kārayitvā udakena pūrayitvā
71.d: सप्त नदीरूपाणि कारयित्वा उदकेन पूरयित्वा

71.s: ā rohata savitur nāvam etāṃ sutrāmāṇaṃ mahīm ū ṣu iti sahiraṇyāṃ sayavāṃ nāvam ārohayati
71.d: आ रोहत सवितुर् नावम् एतां सुत्रामाणं महीम् ऊ षु इति सहिरण्यां सयवां नावम् आरोहयति

71.s: aśmanvatī rīyate ut tiṣṭhatā pra taratā sakhāyo ity udīcas tārayati
71.d: अश्मन्वती रीयते उत् तिष्ठता प्र तरता सखायो इत्य् उदीचस् तारयति

72.s: uttarato garta udakprasravaṇe aśmāna nidadhāty antaśchinnam
72.d: उत्तरतो गर्त उदक्प्रस्रवणे अश्मान निदधात्य् अन्तश्छिन्नम्
72.m:
[72].1) To the north, in a pit running northwards, he deposits a severed stone.
[72].2) With "Beyond death…" [AVŚ 12.2.23d], he steps over the stone.
[72].3) With "Those northward from below…" [AVŚ 12.2.41], he consecrates [the cows].
[72].4) Having besprinkled the entry into the house with "Driving out…" [AVŚ 2.14.1],
[72].5) with "Bearing vigor…" [AVŚ 7.60.1], he makes [the householder] enter.
[72].6) With "To the All-gods…" [AVŚ 12.2.28], he causes him to touch a heifer.
[72].7) With "This Indra…" [AVŚ 12.2.47], [he causes him to touch] a bull.
[72].8) With "The draft-ox…" [AVŚ 12.2.48] and "Day and night…" [AVŚ 12.2.49], he causes him to touch the couch.
[72].9) With "Ascend to life…" [AVŚ 12.2.24], he ascends [the couch].
[72].10) With "Seated…" [AVŚ 12.2.30c], he addresses [his wife] who is seated.
[72].11) Having dipped stalks of grass with collyrium into ghee, he hands them to the women with "These women…" [AVŚ 12.2.31].
[72].12) With "These living, unwidowed, good sisters…", he hands them to the men, three to each one, wrapping them all around over the water-jar.
[72].13) With "Away, O Death…" [AVŚ 12.2.21], "I separate…" [AVŚ 12.2.32], "Ascend…" [AVŚ 12.2.24], "Covering…" [AVŚ 12.2.44], "Turning backward the sun…" [AVŚ 12.2.55], "Whatever fires…" [AVŚ 3.21.1], "Homage to the divine slayers…" [AVŚ 6.13.1], "O Agni, returning…" [PS 1.41.1], "O Agni Jātavedas…" [PS 1.41.2], "With wealth…" [PS 1.41.3], [and] "Again with vigor…" [PS 1.41.4]—
[72].14) "O Agni, turning back, turn back toward us with life, with splendor, with gain, with wisdom, with offspring, with wealth! / O Agni Jātavedas, a hundred are your returns, a thousand are your returns; then, being lord of nourishment, bring us wealth again! / Turn back with wealth, O Agni; swell with a stream that nourishes all, from every side! / Turn back again with vigor, O Agni, again with food and life; protect us again from distress!"—
[72].15) he ties naturally-perforated pebbles with hemp ropes and holds them.
[72].16) He offers [ghee] through the middle of the hole.
[72].17) With "This for the living…" [AVŚ 12.2.23], he places [a stone] at the doorway.
[72].18) He makes an offering with this verse: "Giver of life, giver of wealth, giver of strength, giver of cattle, giver of nourishment, to Prajāpati svāhā!"
[72].19) The mother feeds the six residues of oblations to her sons;
[72].20) the remainder to the wife.
[72].21) For a year, he should not let the fire go out, he should not remove it, nor should they remove it.
[72].22) For twelve nights, say some.
[72].23) Ten [cows] are the sacrificial fee.
[72].24) Restraining his speech, he lies down behind the fire.
[72].25) And on the next day, he should sacrifice to Indra and Agni.
[72].26) On the full moon day, [he sacrifices] to Agni and Agni-Soma with two boiled grain offerings.
[72].27) In the evening and morning, he should pour in grains of rice or barley: in the evening with "To Agni svāhā; to Prajāpati svāhā";
[72].28) in the morning with "To Sūrya svāhā; to Prajāpati svāhā".
[72].29) At the end of twelve nights, he should sacrifice to Agni with an animal.
[72].30) Or with a boiled grain offering, [if he fears that] one of the two will fail.
[72].31) On the completion of the year, having prepared pacifying water,
[72].32) reciting "Be an offering of ghee to us, O Agni, not an offering of raw flesh! May we sit down near you as an offering of ghee, not an offering of raw flesh, O Jātavedas!", having gathered four residues of oblations into the water vessel,
[72].33) having skimmed them off,
[72].34) seated to the east of the fire, facing west, he makes an offering with: "Take hold when the offering is made, be a sharer in the offering; be gracious to us, and do not harm our cattle!"
[72].35) If [the fire] should go out, having touched the kindling stick with ashes, having churned it silently and kindled it,
[72].36) having offered a full oblation,
[72].37) he should offer ghee with the saṃnati formulas or with the vyāhṛtis.
[72].38) And in the same way he should offer if [the domestic fire] has become mixed [with another].
[72].39) When the fire is dying out,
[72].40) having smeared around the fire-hearths with a lump of bull-dung,
[72].41) having set down what is to be offered,
[72].42) he should offer into himself with: "To out-breath and in-breath, svāhā! To equalizing breath and diffused breath, svāhā! To the forms of upward breath, svāhā!"
[72].43) Then, having risen in the morning, having churned out the fire, having brought it forward to its proper place, he should offer the Agnihotra as before.
[72].44) The evening and morning meals are the two sacrifices, the two priests.

72.s: piñjūlīr āñjanaṃ sarpiṣi paryasya imā nārīr iti strībhyaḥ prayachati
72.d: पिञ्जूलीर् आञ्जनं सर्पिषि पर्यस्य इमा नारीर् इति स्त्रीभ्यः प्रयछति

72.s: ime jīvā avidhavāḥ sujāmaya iti puṃbhya eka ekasmai tisrastisras tā adhyadhy udadhānaṃ paricṛtya prayachati
72.d: इमे जीवा अविधवाः सुजामय इति पुंभ्य एक एकस्मै तिस्रस्तिस्रस् ता अध्यध्य् उदधानं परिचृत्य प्रयछति

72.s: paraṃ mṛtyo vyākaromi ā rohata antardhir pratyañcam arkaṃ ye agnayo namo devavadhebhyo agne 'bhyāvartinn agne jātavedaḥ saha rayyā punar ūrjā iti
72.d: परं मृत्यो व्याकरोमि आ रोहत अन्तर्धिर् प्रत्यञ्चम् अर्कं ये अग्नयो नमो देववधेभ्यो अग्ने ऽभ्यावर्तिन्न् अग्ने जातवेदः सह रय्या पुनर् ऊर्जा इति

72.s: agne 'bhyāvartinn abhi na ā vavṛtsva | āyuṣā varcasā sanyā medhayā prajayā dhanena || agne jātavedaḥ śataṃ te sahasraṃ ta upāvṛtaḥ | adhā puṣṭasyeśānaḥ punar no rayim ā kṛdhi || saha rayyā ni vartasvāgne pinvasva dhārayā | viśvapsnyā viśvatas pari || punar ūrjā vavṛtsva punar agna iṣāyuṣā | punar naḥ pāhy aṃhasaḥ |
72.d: अग्ने ऽभ्यावर्तिन्न् अभि न आ ववृत्स्व । आयुषा वर्चसा सन्या मेधया प्रजया धनेन ॥ अग्ने जातवेदः शतं ते सहस्रं त उपावृतः । अधा पुष्टस्येशानः पुनर् नो रयिम् आ कृधि ॥ सह रय्या नि वर्तस्वाग्ने पिन्वस्व धारया । विश्वप्स्न्या विश्वतस् परि ॥ पुनर् ऊर्जा ववृत्स्व पुनर् अग्न इषायुषा । पुनर् नः पाह्य् अंहसः ।

72.s: juhoti etayā ṛcā | āyurdāvā dhanadhāvā baladāvā paśudāvā puṣṭidāvā prajāpataye svāhā iti
72.d: जुहोति एतया ऋचा । आयुर्दावा धनधावा बलदावा पशुदावा पुष्टिदावा प्रजापतये स्वाहा इति

72.s: saṃvatsaram agniṃ na udvāyāt na haret nāhareyuḥ
72.d: संवत्सरम् अग्निं न उद्वायात् न हरेत् नाहरेयुः

72.s: sāyaṃprātar vrīhīn āvaped yavān vā agnaye svāhā prajāpataye svāhā iti sāyam
72.d: सायंप्रातर् व्रीहीन् आवपेद् यवान् वा अग्नये स्वाहा प्रजापतये स्वाहा इति सायम्

72.s: sūryāya svāhā prajāpataye svāha iti prātaḥ
72.d: सूर्याय स्वाहा प्रजापतये स्वाह इति प्रातः

72.s: ghṛtāhutir no bhavāgne akravyāhutir ghṛtāhutiṃ tvā vayam akravyāhutim upa ni ṣadema jātavedaḥ iti catura udapātre saṃpātān ānīya
72.d: घृताहुतिर् नो भवाग्ने अक्रव्याहुतिर् घृताहुतिं त्वा वयम् अक्रव्याहुतिम् उप नि षदेम जातवेदः इति चतुर उदपात्रे संपातान् आनीय

72.s: purastād agneḥ pratyaṅ āsīno juhoti | hute rabhasva hutabhāga edhi mṛḍāsmabhyaṃ mota hiṃsīḥ paśūn naḥ iti
72.d: पुरस्ताद् अग्नेः प्रत्यङ् आसीनो जुहोति । हुते रभस्व हुतभाग एधि मृडास्मभ्यं मोत हिंसीः पशून् नः इति

72.s: yady udvāyād bhasmanāraṇiṃ saṃspṛśya tūṣṇīṃ mathitvā uddīpya
72.d: यद्य् उद्वायाद् भस्मनारणिं संस्पृश्य तूष्णीं मथित्वा उद्दीप्य

72.s: prāṇāpānābhyāṃ svahā samānavyānābhyāṃ svāhā udānarūpābhyāṃ svāhā ity ātmani eva juhuyāt
72.d: प्राणापानाभ्यां स्वहा समानव्यानाभ्यां स्वाहा उदानरूपाभ्यां स्वाहा इत्य् आत्मनि एव जुहुयात्

72.s: atha prātar utthāyāgniṃ nirmathya yathāsthānaṃ praṇīya yathāpuram agnihotraṃ juhuyāt
72.d: अथ प्रातर् उत्थायाग्निं निर्मथ्य यथास्थानं प्रणीय यथापुरम् अग्निहोत्रं जुहुयात्

73.s: purodayād astamayāc ca pāvakaṃ prabodhayed gṛhiṇī śuddhahastā | samatīte saṃdhivarṇe 'tha hāvayet susamiddhe pāvaka āhutīṣahiḥ
73.d: पुरोदयाद् अस्तमयाच् च पावकं प्रबोधयेद् गृहिणी शुद्धहस्ता । समतीते संधिवर्णे ऽथ हावयेत् सुसमिद्धे पावक आहुतीषहिः
73.m: [73.1] 'Before sunrise and sunset, the housewife, her hands washed clean, should kindle the fire. Then, when the color of twilight has passed and the fire is well kindled, she should cause [him] to offer, enduring the oblations: / [73.2] To Agni and Prajāpati at night, and to Āditya and Prajāpati by day. Water and firewood sticks are best offered first at every homa sacrifice. / [73.3] With sacrificial firewood sticks, with milk, with a boiled oblation, or with ghee—the evening and morning homa sacrifice is accomplished with even one of these. / [73.4] If the fire, after being taken out and offered into, goes out through negligence, he should churn [fire] and offer the Vyāhṛtis and two full oblations, according to the officiating priests.' / [73.5] That water is poured out eastward with: 'To the forest trees, to the plants born of trees, to the herbs, to the climbing plants, to all the gods, to the divine folk, to the holy folk.' / [73.6] To the south with: 'Svadhā to the great-grandfathers, svadhā to the grandfathers, svadhā to the ancestors.' / [73.7] To the west with: 'To Tārkṣya Ariṣṭanemi; immortality for me!' / [73.8] To the north with: 'To Soma, to the Seven Ṛṣis.' / [73.9] 'On the new or full moon day, after [the place] is swept clean and smeared, he should cause food sacred to the Lord of Vows to be offered into the fire; having given more and himself eaten little, in the afternoon he undertakes the sacrificial vow: / [73.10] Fasting and celibacy, pure, fragrant, he lies down on the ground beside the fire. / [73.11] On the full moon day [an offering] to Agni and Soma; on the new moon day to Indra and Agni; but the previous [offering] to Agni is constant, [and] the subsequent supplementary offering is to Prajāpati. / [73.12] A half-oblation to Sviṣṭakṛt is prescribed for all sacrificial oblations; or it belongs to Anumati among the boiled oblations of the Atharvans. / [73.13] And both Vaiśvadeva offerings produced at the junctures of day and night, according to the officiating priests: these sacrifices are provided with sacrificial grass, with ghee, and with sacrificial fees, except / [73.14] according to ability, according to strength. / Some are eaters of offerings, others are non-eaters of offerings; both approach the Vaiśvadeva oblation. / May they, gathering together, rejoice here; sacrificers, desire refreshment and vigor!' / [73.15] 'O All-gods, O Ādityas, attend upon this sacrificial oblation! / May I not stumble in this sacrifice; it is prepared as an oblation for immortality.' / [73.16] 'He offers of the Vaiśvadeva oblation evening and morning; both of these sacrifices are handed down as the evening meal and the morning meal. / [73.17] The two Vaiśvadeva [offerings] must always be performed by a knower, before eating, pure, [as] the best of sacrifices. Neither one who is not learned in the Veda, nor one with unwashed hands, nor one ignorant of mantras, nor one unlearned should offer. / [73.18] For the gods shrink from impurity and desire purity; they do not relish the sacrificial oblation of one without faith. One should have it offered only by a Brāhmaṇa who knows the Veda; that which is offered by a woman or offered by a Śūdra does not reach the gods. / [73.19] But whoever knows the two ghee-portions, the sacrifices, the procedure of the mantras, the knowledge of the deities, the ritual procedure, and the benedictions—[such] a rite performed by a woman, they say, is not prohibited.'

73.s: agnaye ca prajāpataye ca rātrāv ādityaś ca divā prajāpatiś ca | udakaṃ ca samidhaś ca homehome puro varam
73.d: अग्नये च प्रजापतये च रात्राव् आदित्यश् च दिवा प्रजापतिश् च । उदकं च समिधश् च होमेहोमे पुरो वरम्

73.s: homyaiḥ samidbhiḥ payasā sthālīpākena sarpiṣā | sāyaṃprātar homa eteṣām ekenāpi sidhyati
73.d: होम्यैः समिद्भिः पयसा स्थालीपाकेन सर्पिषा । सायंप्रातर् होम एतेषाम् एकेनापि सिध्यति

73.s: abhyuddhṛto huto 'gniḥ pramādād upaśāmyati | mathite vyāhṛtīr juhuyāt pūrṇahomau yathaṛtvijau
73.d: अभ्युद्धृतो हुतो ऽग्निः प्रमादाद् उपशाम्यति । मथिते व्याहृतीर् जुहुयात् पूर्णहोमौ यथऋत्विजौ

73.s: vanaspatibhyo vānaspatebhya oṣadhibhyo vīrudbhyaḥ sarvebhyo devebhyo devajanebhyaḥ puṇyajanebhyaḥ iti prācīnaṃ tad udakaṃ ninīyate
73.d: वनस्पतिभ्यो वानस्पतेभ्य ओषधिभ्यो वीरुद्भ्यः सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो देवजनेभ्यः पुण्यजनेभ्यः इति प्राचीनं तद् उदकं निनीयते

73.s: svadhā prapitāmahebhyaḥ svadhā pitāmahebhyaḥ svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ iti dakṣiṇataḥ
73.d: स्वधा प्रपितामहेभ्यः स्वधा पितामहेभ्यः स्वधा पितृभ्यः इति दक्षिणतः

73.s: parimṛṣṭe parilipte ca parvaṇi vrātapataṃ hāvayed annam agnau | bhūyo dattvā svayam alpaṃ ca bhuktvāparāhṇe vratam upaiti yājñikam
73.d: परिमृष्टे परिलिप्ते च पर्वणि व्रातपतं हावयेद् अन्नम् अग्नौ । भूयो दत्त्वा स्वयम् अल्पं च भुक्त्वापराह्णे व्रतम् उपैति याज्ञिकम्

73.s: anaśanaṃ brahmacaryaṃ ca bhūmau śucir agnim upaśete sugandhiḥ
73.d: अनशनं ब्रह्मचर्यं च भूमौ शुचिर् अग्निम् उपशेते सुगन्धिः

73.s: agnīṣomābhyāṃ darśana indrāgnibhyām adarśane | āgneyaṃ tu pūrvaṃ nityam anvāhāryaṃ prajāpateḥ
73.d: अग्नीषोमाभ्यां दर्शन इन्द्राग्निभ्याम् अदर्शने । आग्नेयं तु पूर्वं नित्यम् अन्वाहार्यं प्रजापतेः

73.s: ardhāhutis tu sauviṣṭakṛtī sarveṣāṃ haviṣāṃ smṛtā | ānumatī vā bhavati sthālīpākeṣv atharvaṇām
73.d: अर्धाहुतिस् तु सौविष्टकृती सर्वेषां हविषां स्मृता । आनुमती वा भवति स्थालीपाकेष्व् अथर्वणाम्

73.s: ubhau ca saṃdhijau yau vaiśvadevau yathaṛtvijau | varjayitvā sabarhiṣaḥ sājyā yajñāḥ sadakṣiṇāḥ
73.d: उभौ च संधिजौ यौ वैश्वदेवौ यथऋत्विजौ । वर्जयित्वा सबर्हिषः साज्या यज्ञाः सदक्षिणाः

73.s: yathāśakti yathābalaṃ hutādo 'nye ahutādo 'nye | vaiśvadevaṃ havir ubhaye saṃ caranti | te samyañca iha mādayantām iṣam ūrjaṃ yajamānā yam ichata
73.d: यथाशक्ति यथाबलं हुतादो ऽन्ये अहुतादो ऽन्ये । वैश्वदेवं हविर् उभये सं चरन्ति । ते सम्यञ्च इह मादयन्ताम् इषम् ऊर्जं यजमाना यम् इछत

73.s: viśve devā idaṃ havir ādityāsaḥ saparyata | asmin yajñe mā vyathiṣy amṛtāya haviṣkṛtam
73.d: विश्वे देवा इदं हविर् आदित्यासः सपर्यत । अस्मिन् यज्ञे मा व्यथिष्य् अमृताय हविष्कृतम्

73.s: vaiśvadevasya haviṣaḥ sāyaṃprātar juhoti | sāyamāśaprātarāśau yajñāv etau smṛtāv ubhau
73.d: वैश्वदेवस्य हविषः सायंप्रातर् जुहोति । सायमाशप्रातराशौ यज्ञाव् एतौ स्मृताव् उभौ

73.s: apratibhuktau śucikāryau ca nityaṃ vaiśvadevau jānatā yajñaśreṣṭhau | nāśrotriyo nānavaniktapāṇir nāmantravij juhuyān nāvipaścit
73.d: अप्रतिभुक्तौ शुचिकार्यौ च नित्यं वैश्वदेवौ जानता यज्ञश्रेष्ठौ । नाश्रोत्रियो नानवनिक्तपाणिर् नामन्त्रविज् जुहुयान् नाविपश्चित्

73.s: bībhatsavaḥ śucikāmā hi devā nāśraddadhānasya havir juṣante | brāhmaṇena brahmavidā tu hāvayen na strīhutaṃ śūdrahutaṃ ca devagam
73.d: बीभत्सवः शुचिकामा हि देवा नाश्रद्दधानस्य हविर् जुषन्ते । ब्राह्मणेन ब्रह्मविदा तु हावयेन् न स्त्रीहुतं शूद्रहुतं च देवगम्

73.s: yas tu vidyād ājyabhāgau yajñān mantraparikramān | devatājñānam āvṛta āśiṣaś ca karma striyā apratiṣiddham āhuḥ
73.d: यस् तु विद्याद् आज्यभागौ यज्ञान् मन्त्रपरिक्रमान् । देवताज्ञानम् आवृत आशिषश् च कर्म स्त्रिया अप्रतिषिद्धम् आहुः

74.m: [74.1] The distribution of tribute offerings for both of them: / [74.2] Having offered with: 'To Agni, to Indra and Agni, to the Lord of the Homestead, to Prajāpati, to Anumati,' / [74.3] having gone out eastward outside, he should distribute tribute offerings copiously with: 'To Brahman, to Vaiśravaṇa, to the All-gods, to all the gods, to all beings, to all creatures.' / [74.4] Besprinkling twice, turning clockwise, having entered inside, at the door— / [74.5] at the two doorposts with: 'To Death, to Dharma and Adharma'; / [74.6] at the water-reservoir for Dhanvantari with: 'To the ocean, to the herbs and forest trees, to Heaven and Earth'; / [74.7] at the pillar and the roof-beam with: 'To the directions, to the intermediate directions'; / [74.8] at the corners with: 'To Vāsuki, to Cittasena, to Cittaratha, to Takṣa and Upatakṣa'; / [74.9] all around the fire with: 'To Hope, to Faith, to Intellect, to Prosperity, to Modesty, to Knowledge'; / [74.10] eastward of the fire with: 'To the domestic divine sisters.' / [74.11] Having taken out more [food], he should feed Brāhmaṇas. / [74.12] A verse also states this: / 'A non-Brāhmaṇa should not eat food prepared in front of him out of desire for food, like poison; a Brāhmaṇa is a god among gods; his name is indeed divinity.' / [74.13] At the first-fruits offering, having prepared pacifying water, having set down rice grains according to the season, / [74.14] having cooked a boiled oblation in water or in milk, / [74.15] there may be either a single sacrificial oblation or various sacrificial oblations with: 'United with the seasons, united with the divisions, united with Agni, svāhā! United with Indra and Agni, united with Heaven and Earth, united with the All-gods, united with the seasons, united with the divisions, united with Soma, svāhā!' / [74.16] [The offering] to Soma consists of wild rice; in autumn it consists of śyāmāka grain. / [74.17] Then the sacrificer takes the portion to be eaten / [74.18] with: 'I take the cup of Prajāpati for my well-being, for my nourishment, for my prosperity, for my modesty, for my fame, for my life, for my food, for my food-eating, for my thousandfold nourishment, for my boundless nourishment.' / [74.19] Then he eats it with: 'The gods have led us together from good to better; by you as nourishment may we enjoy you; enter into us, O food, full of sweetness; come to us as benevolent to our offspring and our bodies!' / [74.20] He recites over what has been eaten: 'You are Amo by name, O breath of life; that truth I speak; you are food, you have entered all my limbs; driving away old age and disease from my body, be painless; may we not come to harm, O Soma juice!' / [74.21] A first-born calf in summer, a garment in autumn is the sacrificial fee. / [74.22] Or he should give the sacrificial fee according to his ability. / [74.23] Exceeding one's ability is not prescribed; exceeding one's ability is not prescribed.

74.s: agnaya indrāgnibhyāṃ vāstoṣpataye prajāpataye 'numataye iti hutvā
74.d: अग्नय इन्द्राग्निभ्यां वास्तोष्पतये प्रजापतये ऽनुमतये इति हुत्वा

74.s: niṣkramya bahiḥ pracīnaṃ brahmaṇe vaiśravaṇāya viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ sarvebhyo devebhyo viśvebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ sarvebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ iti bahuśo baliṃ haret
74.d: निष्क्रम्य बहिः प्रचीनं ब्रह्मणे वैश्रवणाय विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो विश्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यः इति बहुशो बलिं हरेत्

74.s: sraktiṣu vāsukaye cittasenāya cittarathāya takṣopatakṣābhyām iti
74.d: स्रक्तिषु वासुकये चित्तसेनाय चित्तरथाय तक्षोपतक्षाभ्याम् इति

74.s: samantam agner āśāyai śraddhāyai medhāyai śriyai hriyai vidyāyai iti
74.d: समन्तम् अग्नेर् आशायै श्रद्धायै मेधायै श्रियै ह्रियै विद्यायै इति

74.s: tad api śloko vadati | mābrāhmaṇa agrataḥ kṛtam aśnīyād viṣavad annam annakāmyā | devānāṃ devo brāhmaṇo bhḥvo nāmaiṣa devatā iti
74.d: तद् अपि श्लोको वदति । माब्राह्मण अग्रतः कृतम् अश्नीयाद् विषवद् अन्नम् अन्नकाम्या । देवानां देवो ब्राह्मणो भ्ःवो नामैष देवता इति

74.s: āgrayaṇe śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā yathartu taṇḍulān upasādya
74.d: आग्रयणे शान्त्युदकं कृत्वा यथर्तु तण्डुलान् उपसाद्य

74.s: sajūr ṛtubhiḥ sajūr vidhābhiḥ sajūr agnaye svāhā | sajūr indrāgnibhyāṃ sajūr dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ sajūr viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ sajūr ṛtubhiḥ sajūr vidhābhiḥ sajūḥ somāya svāhā ity ekahavir vā syāt nānāhavīṃṣi vā
74.d: सजूर् ऋतुभिः सजूर् विधाभिः सजूर् अग्नये स्वाहा । सजूर् इन्द्राग्निभ्यां सजूर् द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां सजूर् विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः सजूर् ऋतुभिः सजूर् विधाभिः सजूः सोमाय स्वाहा इत्य् एकहविर् वा स्यात् नानाहवींषि वा

74.s: prajāpateṣ ṭvā grahaṃ gṛhṇāmi | mahyaṃ bhūtyai mahyaṃ puṣṭyai mahyaṃ śriyai mahyaṃ hriyai mahyaṃ yaśase mahyam āyuṣe mahyam annāya mahyam annādyāya mahyaṃ sahasrapoṣāya mahyam aparimitapoṣāya iti
74.d: प्रजापतेष् ट्वा ग्रहं गृह्णामि । मह्यं भूत्यै मह्यं पुष्ट्यै मह्यं श्रियै मह्यं ह्रियै मह्यं यशसे मह्यम् आयुषे मह्यम् अन्नाय मह्यम् अन्नाद्याय मह्यं सहस्रपोषाय मह्यम् अपरिमितपोषाय इति

74.s: atha prāśnāti | bhadrān naḥ śreyaḥ sam anaiṣṭa devās tvayāvasena sam aśīmahi tvā | sa naḥ pito madhumā;m ā viveśa śivas tokāya tanvo na ehi iti
74.d: अथ प्राश्नाति । भद्रान् नः श्रेयः सम् अनैष्ट देवास् त्वयावसेन सम् अशीमहि त्वा । स नः पितो मधुमा;म् आ विवेश शिवस् तोकाय तन्वो न एहि इति

74.s: prāśitam anumantrayate | amo 'si prāṇa tad ṛtaṃ bravīmy amāsi sarvāṅ asi praviṣṭa | sa me jarāṃ rogam apanudya śarīrādanāmayaidhi mā riṣāma indo iti
74.d: प्राशितम् अनुमन्त्रयते । अमो ऽसि प्राण तद् ऋतं ब्रवीम्य् अमासि सर्वाङ् असि प्रविष्ट । स मे जरां रोगम् अपनुद्य शरीरादनामयैधि मा रिषाम इन्दो इति

74.s: vatsaḥ prathamajo grīṣme vāsaḥ śaradi dakṣiṇā
74.d: वत्सः प्रथमजो ग्रीष्मे वासः शरदि दक्षिणा

75.m:
[75].1) Now, the marriage rite.
[75].2) From the full moon day of Kārttika until that of Vaiśākha,
[75].3) or according to desire.
[75].4) But one should avoid the fortnight of Citrā.
[75].5) "Under the Maghās the cows are slain; under the Phalgunīs [the bride] is led home"—thus it is known [from sacred tradition], and [there is] an auspicious day.
[75].6) With "Upheld by truth..." and "The prior and posterior..." he places [the two wedding garments].
[75].7) And [he recites the hymn for] finding a husband.
[75].8) With "You two, O Bhaga..." he sends forth the wooer together with an attendant,
[75].9) [and] with "O Brahmaṇaspati..." the Brahman priest.
[75].10) Fearing that tearing-apart, at night, having kindled wood shavings from the girl's family,
[75].11) with the five [verses beginning with] "The gods at first..." he causes roasted grains to be poured out once.
[75].12) With "Free from thorns..." he dispatches the guardian of the girl.
[75].13) In front of the water-carrier is [a man] with an arrow set [on his bow], behind him the Brahman priest.
[75].14) With "The one that is without firewood..." he throws a clod of earth into the water.
[75].15) With "This I [cast away]..." having pushed [the water] aside,
[75].16) with "The auspicious one..." having drawn out [water] along the current,
[75].17) with "O Brahmins, for her..." he hands it over.
[75].18) As they return, the Brahman priest walks in front, behind walks the man with a strung bow.
[75].19) Outside, to the north of the fire, he hangs [the water vessel] on a branch of a waved-leaf fig or cluster fig tree.
[75].20) With that [water] they perform the rites requiring water.
[75].21) And then [follows] the subsequent pouring [of water] with other [water].
[75].22) Having stepped inside, he offers an oblation with "Aryaman...".
[75].23) With "I untie you..." he unties the head-band.
[75].24) With this [verse] "Desiring..." he makes her put on [garments] three times.
[75].25) With seven [verses] he makes warm waters endowed with the residue of oblations.
[75].26) With "What on the chair..." he bathes her as she stands at the northern of the two eastern corners.
[75].27) With "And what lustre..." and "As the river..." he pours over her, when she has stepped out, with other [water].

75.s: maghāsu hanyante gāvaḥ phalgunīṣu vyuhyate iti vijñāyate maṅgalaṃ ca
75.d: मघासु हन्यन्ते गावः फल्गुनीषु व्युह्यते इति विज्ञायते मङ्गलं च

75.s: yuvaṃ bhagaṃ iti saṃbhalaṃ sānucaraṃ prahiṇoti
75.d: युवं भगं इति संभलं सानुचरं प्रहिणोति

75.s: tad vivṛhāt śaṅkamāno niśi kumārīkulād valīkāni ādīpya
75.d: तद् विवृहात् शङ्कमानो निशि कुमारीकुलाद् वलीकानि आदीप्य

75.s: devā agre iti pañcabhiḥ sakṛt pūlyāni āvāpayati
75.d: देवा अग्रे इति पञ्चभिः सकृत् पूल्यानि आवापयति

75.s: yo anidhmo ity apsu logaṃ pravidhyati
75.d: यो अनिध्मो इत्य् अप्सु लोगं प्रविध्यति

75.s: bāhyataḥ plakṣodumbarasya uttarato agneḥ śākhāyām āsajati
75.d: बाह्यतः प्लक्षोदुम्बरस्य उत्तरतो अग्नेः शाखायाम् आसजति

75.s: pra tvā muñcāmi iti veṣṭaṃ vicṛtati
75.d: प्र त्वा मुञ्चामि इति वेष्टं विचृतति

75.s: yad āsandyām iti pūrvayor uttarasyāṃ sraktyāṃ tiṣṭhantīm āplāvayati
75.d: यद् आसन्द्याम् इति पूर्वयोर् उत्तरस्यां स्रक्त्यां तिष्ठन्तीम् आप्लावयति

75.s: yac ca varco yathā sindhur ity utkrāntām anyenāvasiñcati
75.d: यच् च वर्चो यथा सिन्धुर् इत्य् उत्क्रान्ताम् अन्येनावसिञ्चति

76.s: yad duṣkṛtaṃ iti vāsasāṅgāni pramṛjya kumārīpālāya prayachati
76.d: यद् दुष्कृतं इति वाससाङ्गानि प्रमृज्य कुमारीपालाय प्रयछति
76.m:
[76].1) With "What evil deed..." having wiped her limbs with a cloth, he gives it to the guardian of the girl.
[76].2) Having taken it on a stick of timber, he should go out.
[76].3) He fastens it in the forest.
[76].4) With "Those who spun..." and "Tvaṣṭṛ [fashioned] the garment..." he clothes her with an unwashed [garment].
[76].5) With "Fashioned..." having combed her once with a hundred-toothed comb made of reed,
[76].6) he throws it down with: "The journey is accomplished."
[76].7) With "Hoping for..." and "I bind you around..." he binds her with a girdle having loops at both ends.
[76].8) With "This plant..." having tied an amulet of licorice with a thread dyed red with lac, he ties it onto the ring-finger.
[76].9) The amulet is at the inner side, the knot at the outer side.
[76].10) With "May Bhaga lead you from here..." having taken her by the hand, he leads her out.
[76].11) Having placed a yoke on a branch, another [man] holds it from the south.
[76].12) Fastened with darbha grass to the southern yoke-pole [and placed] over the northern yoke-hole, supporting a piece of gold at her forehead with "Propitious for you..." he recites the formula.
[76].13) He pours [water] directly through the hole.
[76].14) Having taken hold of her to the north of the fire, he pours out [the water] with "From limb to limb...".
[76].15) With "Pleasant..." he places a stone upon a lump of dung.
[76].16) With "Step upon it..." having made her mount it,
[76].17) with "This woman..." he causes her, standing firm, to pour out roasted grains,
[76].18) three times without interruption, [and] a fourth time for desire.
[76].19) With "With which Agni..." he takes her hand.
[76].20) With "Of Aryaman..." he leads her around the fire three times.
[76].21) With "Seven boundaries..." he draws seven lines to the north of the fire, directed eastward.
[76].22) He makes her take steps upon them.
[76].23) "For sap, O auspicious one, rich in offspring, full of coolness!" is the first [formula].
[76].24) "For vigor... for increase of wealth... for good fortune... for sovereignty... for abundance... for long life, O auspicious one, rich in offspring, full of coolness!" is the seventh; "Be a friend [at the completion of] seven steps."
[76].25) With "Mount the couch..." and "Bhaga fashioned..." he seats her upon the couch.
[76].26) When she is seated, a friend washes her feet.
[76].27) While they are being washed, he accompanies them with the formula: "These two feet, fortunate, very kind, may they work for our good fortune, not for evil; being washed, the fortunate [feet] of the good wife, may they bestow offspring, cattle, and long life."
[76].28) With "I untie..." and "I release you..." he loosens the girdle.
[76].29) In the subsequent [contest], the servants engage in a struggle.
[76].30) Those who conquer are regarded as the stronger indeed.
[76].31) With "By Bṛhaspati..." verse by verse, he pours all-fragrant powders on her head with a Kāmpīla leaf.
[76].32) With "Raise up...", "Bhaga fashioned...", and "Not slaying her brother..." he raises her up, verse by verse.
[76].33) With "Stand firm..." he establishes her firmly.

76.s: tumbaradaṇḍena pratipādya nirvrajet
76.d: तुम्बरदण्डेन प्रतिपाद्य निर्व्रजेत्

76.s: tad vana āsajati
76.d: तद् वन आसजति

76.s: yā akṛntaṃs tvaṣṭā vāso ity ahatenāchāyati
76.d: या अकृन्तंस् त्वष्टा वासो इत्य् अहतेनाछायति

76.s: kṛtrimaḥ iti śatadatā iṣīkeṇa kaṅkatena sakṛt pralikhya
76.d: कृत्रिमः इति शतदता इषीकेण कङ्कतेन सकृत् प्रलिख्य

76.s: kṛtayāmam ity avasṛjati
76.d: कृतयामम् इत्य् अवसृजति

76.s: āśāsānā saṃ tvā nahyāmi ity ubhayataḥ pāśena yoktreṇa saṃnahyati
76.d: आशासाना सं त्वा नह्यामि इत्य् उभयतः पाशेन योक्त्रेण संनह्यति

76.s: iyaṃ vīrud iti madughamaṇiṃ lākṣāraktena sūtreṇa vigrathyānāmikāyāṃ badhnāti
76.d: इयं वीरुद् इति मदुघमणिं लाक्षारक्तेन सूत्रेण विग्रथ्यानामिकायां बध्नाति

76.s: antato ha maṇir bhavati bāhyo granthiḥ
76.d: अन्ततो ह मणिर् भवति बाह्यो ग्रन्थिः

76.s: bhagas tveto iti hastegṛhya nirṇayati
76.d: भगस् त्वेतो इति हस्तेगृह्य निर्णयति

76.s: śākhāyāṃ yugam ādhāya dakṣiṇato anyo dhārayati
76.d: शाखायां युगम् आधाय दक्षिणतो अन्यो धारयति

76.s: dakṣiṇasyāṃ yugadhuri uttarasmin yugatardmani darbheṇa vigrathya śaṃ te iti lalāṭe hiraṇyaṃ saṃstabhya japati
76.d: दक्षिणस्यां युगधुरि उत्तरस्मिन् युगतर्द्मनि दर्भेण विग्रथ्य शं ते इति ललाटे हिरण्यं संस्तभ्य जपति

76.s: tardma samayāvasiñcati
76.d: तर्द्म समयावसिञ्चति

76.s: upagṛhya uttarato agner aṅgādaṅgād iti ninayati
76.d: उपगृह्य उत्तरतो अग्नेर् अङ्गादङ्गाद् इति निनयति

76.s: syonaṃ iti śakṛtpiṇḍe aśmānaṃ nidadhāti
76.d: स्योनं इति शकृत्पिण्डे अश्मानं निदधाति

76.s: tam ā tiṣṭha ity āsthāpya
76.d: तम् आ तिष्ठ इत्य् आस्थाप्य

76.s: iyaṃ nārī iti dhruvāṃ tiṣṭhantīṃ pūlyāni āvāpayati
76.d: इयं नारी इति ध्रुवां तिष्ठन्तीं पूल्यानि आवापयति

76.s: trir avichindatīṃ caturthīṃ kāmāya
76.d: त्रिर् अविछिन्दतीं चतुर्थीं कामाय

76.s: yenāgnir iti pāṇiṃ grāhayati
76.d: येनाग्निर् इति पाणिं ग्राहयति

76.s: aryamṇo ity agniṃ triḥ pariṇayati
76.d: अर्यम्णो इत्य् अग्निं त्रिः परिणयति

76.s: sapta maryādāḥ ity uttarato agneḥ sapta lekhā likhati prācyaḥ
76.d: सप्त मर्यादाः इत्य् उत्तरतो अग्नेः सप्त लेखा लिखति प्राच्यः

76.s: tāsu padāni utkrāmayati
76.d: तासु पदानि उत्क्रामयति

76.s: iṣe tvā sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīma iti prathamam
76.d: इषे त्वा सुमङ्गलि प्रजावति सुशीम इति प्रथमम्

76.s: ūrje tvā rāyaspoṣāya tvā saubhāgyāya tvā sāmrājyāya tvā saṃpade tvā jīvātave tvā sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīma iti saptamaṃ sakhā saptapadī bhava iti
76.d: ऊर्जे त्वा रायस्पोषाय त्वा सौभाग्याय त्वा साम्राज्याय त्वा संपदे त्वा जीवातवे त्वा सुमङ्गलि प्रजावति सुशीम इति सप्तमं सखा सप्तपदी भव इति

76.s: ā roha talpaṃ bhagas tatakṣa iti talpa upaveśayati
76.d: आ रोह तल्पं भगस् ततक्ष इति तल्प उपवेशयति

76.s: upaviṣṭāyāḥ suhṛtpādau prakṣālayati
76.d: उपविष्टायाः सुहृत्पादौ प्रक्षालयति

76.s: prakṣālyamānau anumantrayate | imau pādau subhagau suśevau saubhāgyāya kṛṇutāṃ no aghāya | prakṣālyamānau subhagau supatnyāḥ prajāṃ paśūn dīrgham āyuś ca dhattām iti
76.d: प्रक्षाल्यमानौ अनुमन्त्रयते । इमौ पादौ सुभगौ सुशेवौ सौभाग्याय कृणुतां नो अघाय । प्रक्षाल्यमानौ सुभगौ सुपत्न्याः प्रजां पशून् दीर्घम् आयुश् च धत्ताम् इति

76.s: ahaṃ vi ṣyāmi pra tvā muñcāmi iti yoktraṃ vicṛtati
76.d: अहं वि ष्यामि प्र त्वा मुञ्चामि इति योक्त्रं विचृतति

76.s: aparasmin bhṛtyāḥ saṃrabhante
76.d: अपरस्मिन् भृत्याः संरभन्ते

76.s: ye jayanti te balīyāṃsa eva manyante
76.d: ये जयन्ति ते बलीयांस एव मन्यन्ते

76.s: bṛhaspatinā iti sarvasurabhicūrṇāni ṛcarcā kāmpīlapalāśena mūrdhni āvapati
76.d: बृहस्पतिना इति सर्वसुरभिचूर्णानि ऋचर्चा काम्पीलपलाशेन मूर्ध्नि आवपति

76.s: ud yachadhvam bhagas tatakṣa abhrātṛghnīṃ ity eka ekayā utthāpayati
76.d: उद् यछध्वम् भगस् ततक्ष अभ्रातृघ्नीं इत्य् एक एकया उत्थापयति

76.s: prati tiṣṭha iti pratiṣṭhāpayati
76.d: प्रति तिष्ठ इति प्रतिष्ठापयति

77.s: sukiṃśukaṃ rukmaprastaraṇaṃ iti yānam ārohayati
77.d: सुकिंशुकं रुक्मप्रस्तरणं इति यानम् आरोहयति
77.m:
[77].1) With "Of good kiṃśuka wood..." [and] "With an overlay of gold...", he causes [the bride] to mount the vehicle.
[77].2) With "[Come] along this path..." [and] "With the Brahman following...", the Brahman priest steps forward in front.
[77].3) With "Let them not find..." [and] "Free from thorns...", [the protection of] the journey has been stated.
[77].4) If another [woman] has been married [first] by him, he stands upon the hem of the wedding garment at a crossroad with his right [foot] with "She who formerly...".
[77].5) If he desires welfare for both, he mutters this verse: "To Sūryā, to the gods...".
[77].6) With "Encounter a good path, not falling away, both [having] pleasant slopes, both ruling, both having good offspring...", they cause [the couple] to walk between, behind the Brahman priest.
[77].7) Having besprinkled the vehicle with "Who, even without attachments...", he drives [it] out.
[77].8) With "She, rejoicing...", he throws a clod of earth at a water-crossing.
[77].9) With "May this well of me...", he mutters at large trees.
[77].10) With "Very auspicious...", he mutters towards those who look at the bride.
[77].11) With "The plants which...", towards the [objects] mentioned in the mantra.
[77].12) With "Those ancestors who...", at cremation grounds.
[77].13) With "Awake...", he should awaken her if she has fallen asleep.
[77].14) With "I display...", he mutters at the sight of the house.
[77].15) Having besprinkled the vehicle with "Up [is] your wave...", he unyokes [it].
[77].16) With "Arise from here...", the wife besprinkles the hall.
[77].17) With "Pleasant...", he places a stone upon a lump of cow dung to the south of the eaves.
[77].18) Above it, upon the middle palāśa leaf, in ghee, [he places] four tips of dūrvā grass.
[77].19) Having caused [her] to step on [it] with "Step upon that...",
[77].20) with "Very auspicious, bringing across...", "Here [be] dear...", "Do not harm...", [and] "With the Brahman following...", verse by verse, he causes [her] to enter.
[77].21) A friend presents [her] with a full metal cup.
[77].22) With "Not having an evil eye...", he leads [her] three times around the fire.
[77].23) With "When the Gārhapatya..." [and] "To Sūryā, to the gods...", he recites over her as she pays obeisance to those mentioned in the mantra.

77.s: emamṃ panthām brahmāparaṃ ity agrato brahmā prapadyate
77.d: एमम्ं पन्थाम् ब्रह्मापरं इत्य् अग्रतो ब्रह्मा प्रपद्यते

77.s: mā vidann anṛkṣarā adhvānam ity uktam
77.d: मा विदन्न् अनृक्षरा अध्वानम् इत्य् उक्तम्

77.s: yedaṃ purvā iti tenānyasyām ūḍhāyāṃ vādhūyasya daśāṃ catuṣpathe dakṣiṇair abhitiṣṭhati
77.d: येदं पुर्वा इति तेनान्यस्याम् ऊढायां वाधूयस्य दशां चतुष्पथे दक्षिणैर् अभितिष्ठति

77.s: sa ced ubhayoḥ śubhakāmo bhavati sūryāyai devebhyo ity etām ṛcaṃ japati
77.d: स चेद् उभयोः शुभकामो भवति सूर्यायै देवेभ्यो इत्य् एताम् ऋचं जपति

77.s: sam ṛchata svapatho 'navayantaḥ suśīmakāmāv ubhe virājāv ubhe suprajasau ity atikramayato 'ntarā brahmāṇam
77.d: सम् ऋछत स्वपथो ऽनवयन्तः सुशीमकामाव् उभे विराजाव् उभे सुप्रजसौ इत्य् अतिक्रमयतो ऽन्तरा ब्रह्माणम्

77.s: ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣaḥ iti yānaṃ saṃprokṣya viniṣkārayati
77.d: य ऋते चिद् अभिश्रिषः इति यानं संप्रोक्ष्य विनिष्कारयति

77.s: sā mandasānā iti tīrthe logaṃ pravidhyati
77.d: सा मन्दसाना इति तीर्थे लोगं प्रविध्यति

77.s: idaṃ su me iti mahāvṛkṣeṣu japati
77.d: इदं सु मे इति महावृक्षेषु जपति

77.s: sumaṅgalīr iti vadhvīkṣīḥ prati japati
77.d: सुमङ्गलीर् इति वध्वीक्षीः प्रति जपति

77.s: yā oṣadhayo iti mantrokteṣu
77.d: या ओषधयो इति मन्त्रोक्तेषु

77.s: ye pitaro iti śmaśāneṣu
77.d: ये पितरो इति श्मशानेषु

77.s: pra budhyasva iti suptāṃ prabodhayet
77.d: प्र बुध्यस्व इति सुप्तां प्रबोधयेत्

77.s: saṃ kāśayāmi iti gṛhasaṃkāśe japati
77.d: सं काशयामि इति गृहसंकाशे जपति

77.s: ud va ūrmiḥ iti yānaṃ saṃprokṣya vimocayati
77.d: उद् व ऊर्मिः इति यानं संप्रोक्ष्य विमोचयति

77.s: ut tiṣṭhetaḥ iti patnī śālāṃ saṃprokṣati
77.d: उत् तिष्ठेतः इति पत्नी शालां संप्रोक्षति

77.s: syonaṃ iti dakṣiṇato valīkānāṃ śakṛtpiṇḍe aśmānaṃ nidadhāti
77.d: स्योनं इति दक्षिणतो वलीकानां शकृत्पिण्डे अश्मानं निदधाति

77.s: tasya upari madhyamapalāśe sarpiṣi catvāri dūrvāgrāṇi
77.d: तस्य उपरि मध्यमपलाशे सर्पिषि चत्वारि दूर्वाग्राणि

77.s: tam ā tiṣṭha ity āsthāpya
77.d: तम् आ तिष्ठ इत्य् आस्थाप्य

77.s: sumaṅgalī prataraṇī iha priyaṃ mā hiṃsiṣṭaṃ brahmāparaṃ iti pratyṛcaṃ prapādayati
77.d: सुमङ्गली प्रतरणी इह प्रियं मा हिंसिष्टं ब्रह्मापरं इति प्रत्यृचं प्रपादयति

77.s: suhṛtpūrṇakaṃsena pratipādayati
77.d: सुहृत्पूर्णकंसेन प्रतिपादयति

77.s: aghoracakṣur ity agniṃ triḥ pariṇayati
77.d: अघोरचक्षुर् इत्य् अग्निं त्रिः परिणयति

77.s: yadā gārhapatyam sūryāyai devebhyo iti mantroktebhyo namaskurvatīm anumantrayate
77.d: यदा गार्हपत्यम् सूर्यायै देवेभ्यो इति मन्त्रोक्तेभ्यो नमस्कुर्वतीम् अनुमन्त्रयते

78.m:
[78].1) [He recites over one] bringing a red hide with "Protection, armor...".
[78].2) [He recites over one] spreading it out with "And spread out the hide...".
[78].3) [He recites over one] placing balbaja grass with "The balbaja which...".
[78].4) [He recites over one] strewing [it] with "Strew upon...".
[78].5) With "Let her mount upon that...", he causes [her] to mount [it].
[78].6) With "Sitting down there...", he causes [her] to sit down.
[78].7) He places his right leg over the left upon his lap.
[78].8) With "Possessing good seniority...", he sits on her lap a son of a Brahmin who has an auspicious name.
[78].9) With "Let them disperse...", having measured a festive portion, he causes [him] to stand up.
[78].10) With "By that being...", "To you in the beginning...", "Adorning...", [and] "Agni, finding people, gave this wife to me; Soma, finding wealth, gave this wife to me; Pūṣan, finding kin, gave this wife to me; Indra, the most powerful, gave this wife to me. To Agni, finding people, svāhā! To Soma, finding wealth, svāhā! To Pūṣan, finding kin, svāhā! To Indra, the most powerful, svāhā!",
[78].11) with "They two arrive..." [and] "Savitṛ of impulses...", he pours residues of oblations upon the heads [of both of them].
[78].12) The subsequent ones into a water vessel.
[78].13) With the "adorning" [verse], he pours out into their joined hands.
[78].14) Eating together [takes place] with "By that being...".
[78].15) He causes [both] to eat ritual fluids and boiled domestic oblation.
[78].16) He sacrifices a full double handful of barley mixed with ghee.

78.s: sujyaiṣṭhyo iti kalyāṇanāmānaṃ brāhmaṇāyanam upastha upaveśayati
78.d: सुज्यैष्ठ्यो इति कल्याणनामानं ब्राह्मणायनम् उपस्थ उपवेशयति

78.s: vi tiṣṭhantāṃ iti pramadanaṃ pramāya utthāpayati
78.d: वि तिष्ठन्तां इति प्रमदनं प्रमाय उत्थापयति

78.s: tena bhūtena tubhyam agre śumbhanī agnir janavin mahyaṃ jāyām imām adāt somo vasuvin mahyaṃ jāyām imām adāt pūṣā jñātivin mahyaṃ jāyām imām adād indraḥ sahīyān mahyaṃ jāyām adād agnaye janavide svāhā somāya vasuvide svāhā pūṣṇe jñātivide svāhendrāya sahīyase svāhā iti
78.d: तेन भूतेन तुभ्यम् अग्रे शुम्भनी अग्निर् जनविन् मह्यं जायाम् इमाम् अदात् सोमो वसुविन् मह्यं जायाम् इमाम् अदात् पूषा ज्ञातिविन् मह्यं जायाम् इमाम् अदाद् इन्द्रः सहीयान् मह्यं जायाम् अदाद् अग्नये जनविदे स्वाहा सोमाय वसुविदे स्वाहा पूष्णे ज्ञातिविदे स्वाहेन्द्राय सहीयसे स्वाहा इति

78.s: āgachataḥ savitā prasavānām iti mūrdhnoḥ saṃpātān ānayati
78.d: आगछतः सविता प्रसवानाम् इति मूर्ध्नोः संपातान् आनयति

79.s: sapta maryādāḥ iti tisṛṇāṃ prātar āvapate
79.d: सप्त मर्यादाः इति तिसृणां प्रातर् आवपते
79.m:
[79].1) With the three [verses beginning with] "The seven boundaries" (AV 5.1.6), he pours in [the seeds] in the morning.
[79].2) With "May our eyes" (AV 7.36.1), the two anoint each other's eyes.
[79].3) With "The great [protection] indeed" (AV 7.6.2), he makes [her] take hold of the bed.
[79].4) With "Mount the bed" (AV 14.2.31), he makes her mount [it].
[79].5) With "Sitting down there" (AV 14.2.23c), he makes her sit down.
[79].6) With "The gods in the beginning" (AV 14.2.32), he makes her lie down.
[79].7) With "Over you" (AV 7.37.1), he covers [her].
[79].8) With "Together, the two parents" (AV 14.2.37), he makes [them] lie down together.
[79].9) With "Here these two" (AV 14.2.64), he pushes [them] together three times.
[79].10) Having removed the licorice-amulet in bovine urine, with "This plant" (AV 1.34.1) and "I am he" (AV 14.2.71), the two touch each other.
[79].11) With "Brahman born first" (AV 4.1.1), he uncovers [her] with the thumb.
[79].12) With "From a pleasant womb" (AV 14.2.43), he raises her up.
[79].13) With the two dressing [verses], he covers [her] with an unwashed garment.
