[79].14) With "Bṛhaspati" (AV 14.1.55), having basted [her head] with ghee using young grass sprouts, having placed rice and barley grains [upon it], he parts the hairline with a bundle of darbha shoots.
[79].15) Having wrapped [her head] with a piece of hemp cloth, they remain asleep for three nights.
[79].16) He should put [firewood sticks] on [the fire] while they hold on to him during the two lessons.
[79].17) With "Here you shall dwell" (AV 14.1.32), having paid the bridal price,
[79].18) he turns [them] away with two [verses, saying], "Here let it succeed for me, there for you."
[79].19) Or as they deem fit.
[79].20) With "Give away" (AV 14.1.25), he consecrates [the bridegroom] giving the bridal garment.
[79].21) With "Given by the gods" (AV 14.2.41), [the recipient] accepts it.
[79].22) With "Away from us the darkness" (AV 14.2.48), he hangs it upon a tree stump.
[79].23) With "As many sorceries" (AV 14.2.49), he should walk away.
[79].24) With "She who is most dear to me" (AV 14.2.50), he covers a tree.
[79].25) Having bathed with the cleansing [hymn],
[79].26) with "Those ends" (AV 14.2.51), he puts on a garment.
[79].27) With "Wearing a new [garment]" (AV 14.2.44), he approaches.
[79].28) Where he would not find "The earlier and the later" (AV 14.1.23), he should use "With the Brahman following" (AV 14.1.64).
[79].29) The sacrificial fee is a cow; [he gives] the returning vehicle.
[79].30) With "They weep for the living" (AV 14.1.46) and "If these hairy ones" (AV 14.2.59), he offers oblations.
[79].31) This is the wedding according to Sūryā.
[79].32) The one with "With the Brahman following" (AV 14.1.64) is according to Brahman.
[79].33) The rites are according to Prajāpati; according to Prajāpati.

79.s: mahīm u ṣu iti talpam ālambhayati
79.d: महीम् उ षु इति तल्पम् आलम्भयति

79.s: madughamaṇim aukṣe apanīya iyaṃ vīrud amo 'ham iti saṃspṛśataḥ
79.d: मदुघमणिम् औक्षे अपनीय इयं वीरुद् अमो ऽहम् इति संस्पृशतः

79.s: bṛhaspatiḥ iti śaṣpeṇābhighārya vrīhiyavābhyām abhinidhāya darbhapiñjulyā sīmantaṃ vicṛtati
79.d: बृहस्पतिः इति शष्पेणाभिघार्य व्रीहियवाभ्याम् अभिनिधाय दर्भपिञ्जुल्या सीमन्तं विचृतति

79.s: śaṇaśakalena pariveṣṭya tisro rātrīḥ prati suptāste
79.d: शणशकलेन परिवेष्ट्य तिस्रो रात्रीः प्रति सुप्तास्ते

79.s: ihed asātha ity etayā śulkam apākṛtya
79.d: इहेद् असाथ इत्य् एतया शुल्कम् अपाकृत्य

79.s: dvābhyāṃ nivartayatīha mama rādhyatām atra tava iti
79.d: द्वाभ्यां निवर्तयतीह मम राध्यताम् अत्र तव इति

79.s: parā dehi iti vādhūyaṃ dadatam anumantrayate
79.d: परा देहि इति वाधूयं ददतम् अनुमन्त्रयते

79.s: yā me priyatamā iti vṛkṣaṃ pratichādayati
79.d: या मे प्रियतमा इति वृक्षं प्रतिछादयति

79.s: pūrvāparaṃ yatra nādhigached brahmāparaṃ iti kuryāt
79.d: पूर्वापरं यत्र नाधिगछेद् ब्रह्मापरं इति कुर्यात्

79.s: jīvaṃ rudanti yadīme keśino iti juhoti
79.d: जीवं रुदन्ति यदीमे केशिनो इति जुहोति

80.m:
[80].1) Now we shall explain the ancestral sacrifice [funeral rite].
[80].2) At the place of cremation and deposition, 'trees around at the time of deposition,' as stated in the Brāhmaṇa.
[80].3) When he becomes weak, having strewn darbha grass on thatch-straw, he lowers him down with 'Be soft to him' [18.2.19].
[80].4) He follows [the passing breath] with mantras as stated in the mantra.
[80].5) He illuminates him with 'What the black [bird has touched]' [18.3.55].
[80].6) When one who has established sacred fires has died, he gathers the ritual equipment:
[80].7) ghee, clotted ghee, a goat, and a cow,
[80].8) a garment as the fifth,
[80].9) gold as the sixth.
[80].10) He does not touch the corpse.
[80].11) He addresses another person who acts [for him] with mantras.
[80].12) He prepares pacifying water, and adds [materials] without [broken] fragments, and from the expulsion hymns.
[80].13) With the pacifying water they cut off the hair of the head, the beard, body hair, and nails.
[80].14) They bathe [him].
[80].15) They anoint [him].
[80].16) They bring garlands.
[80].17) Him, thus bathed and adorned, he covers with an unwashed garment with fringes hanging downward, with 'This god for you...' [18.4.31] [and] 'This garment has now first reached you...' [18.2.57a].
[80].18) He offers into the fires with 'Away from this...' [18.2.27].
[80].19) They make pots.
[80].20) They smear them inside with cow dung, or fill them with dry [dung].
[80].21) They heat them separately with the fires, until the cow dung ignites.
[80].22) The order of conveying them is: the āhavanīya fire first, then the dakṣiṇāgni fire, then the gārhapatya fire.
[80].23) Now, if one dies abroad, they transfer the fires separately onto the kindling sticks with 'Climb the mother, O Jātavedas' [18.4.1].
[80].24) Upon them he acts as stated.
[80].25) Or rather, he offers the Agnihotra until cremation with milk of a cow that has another's calf, or milk of an uncalved cow, or with a groats-mash stirred with a single twig.
[80].26) At the new and full moon offerings, [it is performed] with black grains, with her ghee, neither within nor without.
[80].27) Straw is the sacrificial grass.
[80].28) Sesame stalks are the kindling sticks.
[80].29) Having set aside the cup-oblations, the two ghee-portions, and the preliminary and concluding oblations,
[80].30) he should offer with formulas ending in 'oṃ' to restrain inhalation and exhalation.
[80].31) Then, for both, he raises him up with 'Arise' [18.3.8].
[80].32) He makes him move forward three times with 'Move forth' [18.3.9], and raises him as many times.
[80].33) In the very same way, having tied a twig to the rear,
[80].34) he yokes two cows or two men with 'I yoke these two' [18.2.56].
[80].35) With 'Arise, go forth' [18.3.8], 'Move forth' [18.3.9], 'Watery' [18.2.48], 'From here these' [18.1.61], 'Agni and Soma' [18.2.53], [and] 'This former' [18.4.44], and with the Hariṇī verses, [and] with the eight verses 'Run past' [18.2.11–18], they should carry [him].
[80].36) With 'This to thee' [18.3.7], [they carry] the fire in front.
[80].37) With 'Knowing, O inviolable cow' [18.3.4], having led the last cow, the fuel, and the fire around,
[80].38) he lays down the body to the north of the fire with 'Be soft to him' [18.2.19].
[80].39) The Adhvaryus perform a supplementary sacrifice.
[80].40) In it, having set aside [the offerings] according to deity, and the preliminary and concluding oblations,
[80].41) he should offer with formulas ending in 'oṃ' to restrain inhalation and exhalation.
[80].42) Then, for both, having prepared pacifying water with 'Depart' [18.1.55] and 'I give' [18.2.37], and having besprinkled the cremation place with a Kāmpīla branch using the two sprinkling formulas,
[80].43) having excavated with 'Let them rise up' [18.1.44], sprinkled, made markings, and sprinkled again, they pile the pyre toward the southeast.
[80].44) He makes the wife lie down beside [the corpse] with 'This woman' [18.3.1].
[80].45) He raises her up with 'Rise up' [18.3.2].
[80].46) Placing in his right hand whatever gold he wore, basting it with ghee, he has it taken away by the eldest son with 'This gold...' [18.4.56].
[80].47) He wipes the right hand with 'Going to heaven...' [18.4.56c].
[80].48) He has taken away from a brāhmaṇa what is mentioned in the mantra, with 'The staff from the hand' [18.2.59];
[80].49) from a kṣatriya, with 'The bow from the hand' [18.2.60];
[80].50) from a vaiśya, with 'The goad...'.
[80].51) With 'This for the ancestors' [18.4.51], he strews darbha grass and pyre-wood.
[80].52) There he should place him face upward with 'The sacrificer has climbed the piled fire' [18.4.14].
[80].53) In each quarter with 'In the eastern quarter thee' [18.3.30].
[80].54) 'Not so,' say the Uparibabhravas.
[80].55) He accompanies with mantras.
[80].56) Then he drops seven pieces of gold into his seven vital breaths with 'Immortal art thou; for immortality, place immortality in him!'

80.s: durbalībhavantaṃ śālātṛṇeṣu darbhān āstīrya syonāsmai bhava ity avarohayati
80.d: दुर्बलीभवन्तं शालातृणेषु दर्भान् आस्तीर्य स्योनास्मै भव इत्य् अवरोहयति

80.s: ājyaṃ ca pṛṣadājyaṃ cājaṃ ca gāṃ ca
80.d: आज्यं च पृषदाज्यं चाजं च गां च

80.s: evaṃsnātam alaṃkṛtam ahatenāvāgdaśena vasanena prachādayati etat te devaḥ etat tvā vāsaḥ prathamaṃ nv āgann iti
80.d: एवंस्नातम् अलंकृतम् अहतेनावाग्दशेन वसनेन प्रछादयति एतत् ते देवः एतत् त्वा वासः प्रथमं न्व् आगन्न् इति

80.s: tāḥ śakṛdābhyantaraṃ limpanti śuṣkeṇa vā pūrayanti
80.d: ताः शकृदाभ्यन्तरं लिम्पन्ति शुष्केण वा पूरयन्ति

80.s: tāḥ pṛthag agnibhiḥ saṃtāpayanti ā śakṛdādīpanāt
80.d: ताः पृथग् अग्निभिः संतापयन्ति आ शकृदादीपनात्

80.s: teṣāṃ haraṇānupūrvam āhavanīyaṃ prathamaṃ tato dakṣiṇāgniṃ tato gārhapatyam
80.d: तेषां हरणानुपूर्वम् आहवनीयं प्रथमं ततो दक्षिणाग्निं ततो गार्हपत्यम्

80.s: atha videśe pretasya ā rohata janitrīṃ jātavedasaḥ iti pṛthag araṇīṣu agnīn samāropayanti
80.d: अथ विदेशे प्रेतस्य आ रोहत जनित्रीं जातवेदसः इति पृथग् अरणीषु अग्नीन् समारोपयन्ति

80.s: apivānyavatsāyā vā saṃdhinīkṣīreṇa ekaśalākena vā manthenāgnihotraṃ juhoti ā dahanāt
80.d: अपिवान्यवत्साया वा संधिनीक्षीरेण एकशलाकेन वा मन्थेनाग्निहोत्रं जुहोति आ दहनात्

80.s: darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ kṛṣṇakataṇḍulānāṃ tasyā ājyena nāntaṃ na bahiḥ
80.d: दर्शपूर्णमासयोः कृष्णकतण्डुलानां तस्या आज्येन नान्तं न बहिः

80.s: atha ubhayor ut tiṣṭha ity utthāpayati
80.d: अथ उभयोर् उत् तिष्ठ इत्य् उत्थापयति

80.s: pra cyavasva iti triḥ saṃhāpayati yāvatkṛtvaś ca utthāpayati
80.d: प्र च्यवस्व इति त्रिः संहापयति यावत्कृत्वश् च उत्थापयति

80.s: imau yunajmi iti gāvau yunakti puruṣau vā
80.d: इमौ युनज्मि इति गावौ युनक्ति पुरुषौ वा

80.s: ut tiṣṭha prehi pra cyavasva udanvatī ita ete agnīṣomā idaṃ pūrvam iti hariṇībhir hareyur ati drava ity aṣṭabhiḥ
80.d: उत् तिष्ठ प्रेहि प्र च्यवस्व उदन्वती इत एते अग्नीषोमा इदं पूर्वम् इति हरिणीभिर् हरेयुर् अति द्रव इत्य् अष्टभिः

80.s: prajānaty aghnye ity jaghanyāṃ gām edham agniṃ pariṇīya
80.d: प्रजानत्य् अघ्न्ये इत्य् जघन्यां गाम् एधम् अग्निं परिणीय

80.s: syonāsmai bhava ity uttarato agneḥ śarīraṃ nidadhāti
80.d: स्योनास्मै भव इत्य् उत्तरतो अग्नेः शरीरं निदधाति

80.s: atha ubhayor apeta dadāmi ity śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā saṃprokṣaṇībhyāṃ kāmpīlaśākhāyā dahanaṃ saṃprokṣya
80.d: अथ उभयोर् अपेत ददामि इत्य् शान्त्युदकं कृत्वा संप्रोक्षणीभ्यां काम्पीलशाखाया दहनं संप्रोक्ष्य

80.s: ud īratām ity uddhatya abhyukṣya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā punar abhyukṣya prāgdakṣiṇam edhaś cinvanti
80.d: उद् ईरताम् इत्य् उद्धत्य अभ्युक्ष्य लक्षणं कृत्वा पुनर् अभ्युक्ष्य प्राग्दक्षिणम् एधश् चिन्वन्ति

80.s: yad ddhiraṇyaṃ bibharti tad dakṣiṇe pāṇau ādhāya ājyenābhighārya jyeṣṭhena putreṇādāpayati idaṃ hiraṇyaṃ iti
80.d: यद् द्धिरण्यं बिभर्ति तद् दक्षिणे पाणौ आधाय आज्येनाभिघार्य ज्येष्ठेन पुत्रेणादापयति इदं हिरण्यं इति

80.s: svargaṃ yataḥ iti dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ nirmārjayati
80.d: स्वर्गं यतः इति दक्षिणं हस्तं निर्मार्जयति

80.s: idaṃ pitṛbhyo iti darbhān edhān stṛṇāti
80.d: इदं पितृभ्यो इति दर्भान् एधान् स्तृणाति

80.s: tatra enam uttānam ādadhīta ījānaś citam ārukṣad agniṃ iti
80.d: तत्र एनम् उत्तानम् आदधीत ईजानश् चितम् आरुक्षद् अग्निं इति

80.s: athāsya saptasu prāṇeṣu sapta hiraṇyaśakalāni avāsyati amṛtam asy amṛtatvāyāmṛtam asmin dhehi iti
80.d: अथास्य सप्तसु प्राणेषु सप्त हिरण्यशकलानि अवास्यति अमृतम् अस्य् अमृतत्वायामृतम् अस्मिन् धेहि इति

81.m: Then, for one who has established the sacred fires, having spread out a black antelope skin with the hair inside upon darbha grass, / [81.2] having placed him thereon face upwards, / [81.3] then, having filled his sacrificial vessels with clotted ghee, they arrange them suitably [upon him]: / [81.4] the juhū spoon in the right hand; / [81.5] the upabhṛt spoon in the left; / [81.6] the dhruvā spoon at the throat; the agnihotra-ladle upon the mouth; the sruva dipping spoon at the nostrils; / [81.7] he consecrates them with the mantras: "The juhū supported the sky..." [AV 18.4.5] and "Ascend, O dhruvā..." [AV 18.4.6]; / [81.8] the vessel for holding the prāśitra portion on the forehead; / [81.9] the iḍā cup on the head with: "O Agni, this cup..." [AV 18.3.53]; / [81.10] the sacrificial cake on the chest with: "The gods the sacrifice..." [AV 18.4.2]; / [81.11] the wooden sword on the right side; the poker on the left; / [81.12] the trough on the belly; / [81.13] the mortar and pestle at the knees; / [81.14] the cart at the hips; / [81.15] between the thighs, the other sacrificial vessels; / [81.16] the winnowing basket at the feet. / [81.17] The earthen vessels they throw into water. / [81.18] The metallic ones they set down. / [81.19] The mill-stone belongs to the son at home. / [81.20] Then, for both [the deceased and his wife], he consecrates the rear cow as it is led around counter-clockwise with: "I saw the young woman..." [AV 18.3.3] and "Knowing, O unslayable one..." [AV 18.3.4]. / [81.21] They seat it toward the south-west, having struck it behind. / [81.22] Having excised the two kidneys from its back, they place them in his two hands with: "Run past the two dogs..." [AV 18.2.11]; / [81.23] the right [kidney] in the right [hand], the left in the left; / [81.24] the heart on the heart. / [81.25] With the omentum possessing seven apertures, they cover the face with: "Agni's armor..." [AV 18.2.58]; / [81.26] the limbs limb by limb, / [81.27] the right [limbs of the cow] upon the right [limbs of the deceased], the left upon the left. / [81.28] Having covered the cow-pen with the hide together with its head and feet attached, / [81.29] he ties the goat to the south with: "The goat is the share..." [AV 18.2.8] and "May they carry you up..." [AV 18.2.22]. / [81.30] He offers upon the chest, in the house, with: "From him indeed were you born; may this one be born from you, such-a-one, svāhā"; / [81.31] in the same way he offers into the fires with: "To Agni svāhā! To Kāma svāhā! To the world svāhā!"; / [81.32] into the southern fire, say some. / [81.33] The youngest sets it ablaze with: "Do not burn him up entirely, O Agni..." [AV 18.2.4], "Burn him gently..." [AV 18.2.36], "Take hold..." [AV 18.3.71], and "Knowing..." [AV 2.34.5]. / [81.34] When it has caught fire, he offers the oblations to Yama with the sruva dipping spoon: "To him who has departed along the great heights..." [AV 18.1.49]; / [81.35] "Yama was the first who found the way for us..." [AV 18.1.50]—these are the first two; / [81.36] "The Aṅgirases, our ancestors, the Navagvas..." [AV 18.1.58]—the seven consecutive verses; / [81.37] "He who died the first of mortals..." [AV 18.3.13] and "Those who are our father's ancestors, who are grandfathers..." [AV 18.2.49]—eleven [verses]. / [81.38] Then the oblations to Sarasvatī: / [81.39] "The pious call upon Sarasvatī..." [AV 18.1.41], "The ancestors call upon Sarasvatī..." [AV 18.1.42], "O Sarasvatī, you who went on the same chariot..." [AV 18.1.43], "O Sarasvatī, in your vows..." [AV 7.68.1], "This oblation rich in ghee is yours, O Sarasvatī..." [AV 7.68.2], and "May Indra, attended by the Maruts, me..." [AV 18.3.25]. / [81.40] The officiant offers to the south in another [fire]. / [81.41] They attend with all [verses], or starting with three; / [81.42] or with the following verses. / [81.43] These are the following verses: / [81.44] beginning with: "Do not burn him up entirely, O Agni..." [AV 18.2.4], excluding: "Release..." [AV 18.2.10], up to: "Possessing a thousand courses..." [AV 18.2.18]. / [81.45] For one who has established the sacred fires, with the fifteen verses beginning: "Ascend the mother, of Jātavedas..." [AV 18.4.1]. / [81.46] He washes his hands with: "May Mitra and Varuṇa place around me..." [AV 18.3.12]. / [81.47] He sips water with: "With splendor me..." [AV 18.3.10]. / [81.48] To the north, the officiant offers into another [fire] with: "May Vivasvat to us..." [AV 18.3.61].

81.s: kaṇṭhe dhruvāṃ mukhe agnihotrahavanīṃ nāsikayoḥ sruvam
81.d: कण्ठे ध्रुवां मुखे अग्निहोत्रहवनीं नासिकयोः स्रुवम्

81.s: tāni anumantrayate juhūr dadhāra dyām dhruva ā roha iti
81.d: तानि अनुमन्त्रयते जुहूर् दधार द्याम् ध्रुव आ रोह इति

81.s: atha ubhayor apaśyaṃ yuvatiṃ prajānaty aghnye iti jaghanyāṃ gāṃ prasavyaṃ pariṇīyamānām anumantrayate
81.d: अथ उभयोर् अपश्यं युवतिं प्रजानत्य् अघ्न्ये इति जघन्यां गां प्रसव्यं परिणीयमानाम् अनुमन्त्रयते

81.s: tasyāḥ pṛṣṭhato vṛkkau uddhārya pāṇyor asyādadhati ati drava śvānau iti
81.d: तस्याः पृष्ठतो वृक्कौ उद्धार्य पाण्योर् अस्यादधति अति द्रव श्वानौ इति

81.s: agner varma iti vapayā saptachidrayā mukhaṃ prachādayanti
81.d: अग्नेर् वर्म इति वपया सप्तछिद्रया मुखं प्रछादयन्ति

81.s: ajo bhāgas ut tvā vahantu iti dakṣiṇato ajaṃ badhnāti
81.d: अजो भागस् उत् त्वा वहन्तु इति दक्षिणतो अजं बध्नाति

81.s: asmād vai tvam ajāyathā ayaṃ tvad adhi jāyatām asau svāhā ity urasi gṛhe juhoti
81.d: अस्माद् वै त्वम् अजायथा अयं त्वद् अधि जायताम् असौ स्वाहा इत्य् उरसि गृहे जुहोति

81.s: tathāgniṣu juhoti agnaye svāhā kāmāya svāhā lokāya svāhā iti
81.d: तथाग्निषु जुहोति अग्नये स्वाहा कामाय स्वाहा लोकाय स्वाहा इति

81.s: mainam agne vi dahaḥ śaṃ tapa ā rabhasva prajānantaḥ iti kaniṣṭha ādīpayati
81.d: मैनम् अग्ने वि दहः शं तप आ रभस्व प्रजानन्तः इति कनिष्ठ आदीपयति

81.s: ādīpte sruveṇa yāmān homān juhoti pareyivāṃsaṃ pravato mahīr iti
81.d: आदीप्ते स्रुवेण यामान् होमान् जुहोति परेयिवांसं प्रवतो महीर् इति

81.s: yamo no gātuṃ prathamo viveda iti dve prathame
81.d: यमो नो गातुं प्रथमो विवेद इति द्वे प्रथमे

81.s: aṅgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā iti saṃhitāḥ sapta
81.d: अङ्गिरसो नः पितरो नवग्वा इति संहिताः सप्त

81.s: yo mamāra prathamo martyānāṃ ye naḥ pituḥ pitaro ye pitāmahā ity ekādaśa
81.d: यो ममार प्रथमो मर्त्यानां ये नः पितुः पितरो ये पितामहा इत्य् एकादश

81.s: sarasvatīṃ devayanto havante sarasvatīṃ pitaro havante sarasvati yā sarathaṃ yayātha sarasvati vrateṣu te idaṃ te havyaṃ ghṛtavat sarasvati indro mā marutvān iti
81.d: सरस्वतीं देवयन्तो हवन्ते सरस्वतीं पितरो हवन्ते सरस्वति या सरथं ययाथ सरस्वति व्रतेषु ते इदं ते हव्यं घृतवत् सरस्वति इन्द्रो मा मरुत्वान् इति

81.s: mainam agne vi daho itiprabhṛti ava sṛja iti varjayitvā sahasranīthāḥ ity ātaḥ
81.d: मैनम् अग्ने वि दहो इतिप्रभृति अव सृज इति वर्जयित्वा सहस्रनीथाः इत्य् आतः

81.s: ā roha janitrīṃ jātavedasaḥ iti pañcadaśabhir āhitāgnim
81.d: आ रोह जनित्रीं जातवेदसः इति पञ्चदशभिर् आहिताग्निम्

81.s: mitrāvaruṇā pari mām adhātām iti pāṇī prakṣālayate
81.d: मित्रावरुणा परि माम् अधाताम् इति पाणी प्रक्षालयते

81.s: vivasvān no ity uttarato anyasminn anuṣṭhātā juhoti
81.d: विवस्वान् नो इत्य् उत्तरतो अन्यस्मिन्न् अनुष्ठाता जुहोति

82.m:
[82.1] The rites begin with the youngest, for those facing east, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, turning to the right.
[82.2] Then he places into the hands of each of them seven gravel-pebbles.
[82.3] Throwing these down one by one with the left, downward-turned hand, they walk away without looking back.
[82.4] He recites over [them] with the apāgha hymn.
[82.5] All walk ahead of the Brahman priest.
[82.6] Reciting "May we not depart..." [AV 13.1.59], at the edge of the water he mutters the vyagha and the apāgha hymns.
[82.7] He pours out [water] behind.
[82.8] The eldest [recites]: "[Untie] the highest [bond]..." [AV 18.4.69].
[82.9] The Brahman [recites]: "Rich in milk..." [AV 18.3.56]. He scatters the stated bunches of grass.
[82.10] Having sipped pacifying water and sprinkled himself, he makes them cross a river with: "Rich in horses..." [AV 18.2.31].
[82.11] Having seen a lunar mansion, he worships it with: "May the appearance and reflection of the lunar mansions protect me!"
[82.12] Having taken firewood sticks of the śamyāka tree, the Brahman mutters in front:
[82.13] "To whose departure the three go along—gods, men, and all cattle—may that divine mind guide us; may good guidance lead us, let us not be given over to our enemy!" Having sipped pacifying water and sprinkled himself,
[82.14] having thoroughly besprinkled the entry to the house with: "Out of the hall..." [AV 2.14.1],
[82.15] he makes them enter [the house] with: "Bearing vigor..." [AV 7.60.1].
[82.16] He makes them touch a river, a cow, fire, and a stone;
[82.17] barley grains with: "You are barley; keep hatred away from us, keep enmity away!";
[82.18] and grains of khalva and khalakula beans with: "You are a khalvaka...".
[82.19] With the vyagha and apāgha hymns he causes the śamyāka firewood sticks to be laid on [the fire].
[82.20] They inhale their smoke.
[82.21] If whatever is seized by the flesh-eating [fire], if on the next day there is not at the end [of the burning an offering] to the flesh-eating [fire], he pours out a sthālīpāka offering into the fire with: "Milking the bright milk from the sky's vault, swelling with food and vigor, you have drunk the lap of the waters; what ancestral offerings you have made while living, let those drip honey for you!"
[82.22] And at the cremation ground, having milked a cow with another calf, he offers upon its back with: "Into Vaiśvānara I offer this oblation...".
[82.23] In her milk;
[82.24] or a sthālīpāka, according to some.
[82.25] Having stirred a porridge with a ladle made of palāśa wood with: "The fires which..." [AV 3.21.1], using two churning sticks made of kāmpīla wood, on the third [day] he makes an offering over the bones.
[82.26] Having apportioned what is specified in the mantras with: "Unto heaven..." [AV 18.3.5] and "Health unto you the frost..." [AV 18.3.60],
[82.27] he sprinkles [the bones] of a brāhmaṇa with [water] mixed with milk, of a kṣatriya with [water] mixed with honey, of a vaiśya with water.
[82.28] He recites over [them] with: "Let loose..." [AV 18.2.10].
[82.29] With: "May not your mind..." [AV 18.2.24] and "Whatever of your limb..." [AV 18.2.26], he collects [the bones]:
[82.30] first from the feet, the skull-bones last.
[82.31] Having gathered them together in an urn and strewn them with all fragrant powders, having raised them with the raising verses, they should carry them off with the hariṇī verses.
[82.32] He deposits [the urn] at the foot of a tree with: "May not the tree..." [AV 18.2.25].
[82.33] With: "Be soft to him..." [AV 18.2.19], [he deposits it] in the earth. Eating food devoid of spices, they perform the rites for three nights;
[82.34] for ten nights, say some;
[82.35] or according to the custom of the family.
[82.36] After the third [night], having cooked a sthālīpāka for Vaivasvata, he offers it with: "Vivasvant [shall protect] us..." [AV 18.3.61];
[82.37] the third [oblation] with the two yuktā verses;
[82.38] the fourth [oblation] addressed to Anumati.
[82.39] Having poured pacifying water onto the remainder and consecrated it with mantras, he causes it to be consumed.
[82.40] With: "Come forth together..." [AV 18.4.49], he receives two cattle.
[82.41] With: "She has come..." [AV 18.4.50], [he receives] a sacrificial fee of at least ten cows.
[82.42] For twelve nights the performer should observe the vow of Yama:
[82.43] wearing a single garment or three garments,
[82.44] eating only sacrificial food,
[82.45] he should bathe in the evening and in the morning,
[82.46] chaste, keeping the vow, he should sleep on the ground,
[82.47] and he should employ benedictory formulas.

82.s: atha eṣāṃ saptasapta śarkarāḥ pāṇiṣu āvapati
82.d: अथ एषां सप्तसप्त शर्कराः पाणिषु आवपति

82.s: tāsām eka ekāṃ savyenāvācīnahastenāvakiranto anavekṣamāṇā vrajanti
82.d: तासाम् एक एकां सव्येनावाचीनहस्तेनावकिरन्तो अनवेक्षमाणा व्रजन्ति

82.s: mā pra gāma iti japanta udakānte vyaghāpaghe japati
82.d: मा प्र गाम इति जपन्त उदकान्ते व्यघापघे जपति

82.s: payasvatīr iti brahmā || uktāḥ piñjūlīr āvapati
82.d: पयस्वतीर् इति ब्रह्मा ॥ उक्ताः पिञ्जूलीर् आवपति

82.s: nakṣatraṃ dṛṣṭvā upatiṣṭhate nakṣatrāṇāṃ mā saṃkāśaś ca pratīkāśaś cāvatām iti
82.d: नक्षत्रं दृष्ट्वा उपतिष्ठते नक्षत्राणां मा संकाशश् च प्रतीकाशश् चावताम् इति

82.s: śāmyākīḥ samidha ādāya agrato brahmā japati
82.d: शाम्याकीः समिध आदाय अग्रतो ब्रह्मा जपति

82.s: yasya trayā gatam anuprayanti devā manuṣyāḥ paśavaś ca sarve | taṃ no devaṃ mano adhi bravītu sunītir no nayatu dviṣate mā radhāma iti śāntyudakenācamyābhyukṣya
82.d: यस्य त्रया गतम् अनुप्रयन्ति देवा मनुष्याः पशवश् च सर्वे । तं नो देवं मनो अधि ब्रवीतु सुनीतिर् नो नयतु द्विषते मा रधाम इति शान्त्युदकेनाचम्याभ्युक्ष्य

82.s: nadīm ālambhayati gām agnim aśmānaṃ ca
82.d: नदीम् आलम्भयति गाम् अग्निम् अश्मानं च

82.s: yavo 'si yavayāsmad dveṣo yavayārātim iti yavān
82.d: यवो ऽसि यवयास्मद् द्वेषो यवयारातिम् इति यवान्

82.s: yadyat kravyād gṛhyed yadi kravyādā nānte 'paredyuḥ | divo nabhaḥ śukraṃ payo duhānā iṣam ūrjaṃ pinvamānāḥ || apāṃ yonim apādhvaṃ svadhā yāś cakṛṣe jīvaṃs tās te santu madhuścutaḥ ity agnau sthālīpākaṃ nipṛṇāti
82.d: यद्यत् क्रव्याद् गृह्येद् यदि क्रव्यादा नान्ते ऽपरेद्युः । दिवो नभः शुक्रं पयो दुहाना इषम् ऊर्जं पिन्वमानाः ॥ अपां योनिम् अपाध्वं स्वधा याश् चकृषे जीवंस् तास् ते सन्तु मधुश्चुतः इत्य् अग्नौ स्थालीपाकं निपृणाति

82.s: ādahane cāpivānyavatsāṃ dohayitvā tasyāḥ pṛṣṭhe juhoti vaiśvānare havir idaṃ juhomi iti
82.d: आदहने चापिवान्यवत्सां दोहयित्वा तस्याः पृष्ठे जुहोति वैश्वानरे हविर् इदं जुहोमि इति

82.s: ye agnayo iti pālāśyā darvyā mantham upamathya kāmpīlībhyām upamanthanībhyāṃ tṛtīyasyām asthīni abhijuhoti
82.d: ये अग्नयो इति पालाश्या दर्व्या मन्थम् उपमथ्य काम्पीलीभ्याम् उपमन्थनीभ्यां तृतीयस्याम् अस्थीनि अभिजुहोति

82.s: upa dyām śaṃ te nīhāro iti mantroktāni avadāya
82.d: उप द्याम् शं ते नीहारो इति मन्त्रोक्तानि अवदाय

82.s: kṣīrotsiktena brāhmaṇasyāvasiñcati madhūtsiktena kṣatriyasya udakena vaiśyasya
82.d: क्षीरोत्सिक्तेन ब्राह्मणस्यावसिञ्चति मधूत्सिक्तेन क्षत्रियस्य उदकेन वैश्यस्य

82.s: mā te mano yat te aṅgam iti saṃcinoti
82.d: मा ते मनो यत् ते अङ्गम् इति संचिनोति

82.s: kalaśe samopya sarvasurabhicūrṇair avakīrya utthāpanībhir utthāpya hariṇībhir hareyuḥ
82.d: कलशे समोप्य सर्वसुरभिचूर्णैर् अवकीर्य उत्थापनीभिर् उत्थाप्य हरिणीभिर् हरेयुः

82.s: mā tvā vṛkṣaḥ iti vṛkṣamūle nidadhāti
82.d: मा त्वा वृक्षः इति वृक्षमूले निदधाति

82.s: syonāsmai bhava iti bhūmau trirātram arasāśinaḥ karmāṇi kurvate
82.d: स्योनास्मै भव इति भूमौ त्रिरात्रम् अरसाशिनः कर्माणि कुर्वते

82.s: ūrdhvaṃ tṛtīyasyā vaivasvataṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā vivasvān no iti juhoti
82.d: ऊर्ध्वं तृतीयस्या वैवस्वतं स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा विवस्वान् नो इति जुहोति

82.s: ā pra cyavethām iti gāvau upayachati
82.d: आ प्र च्यवेथाम् इति गावौ उपयछति

83.m:
[83].1) Intending to deposit the ancestors [the bones], he gathers the ritual equipment.
[83].2) He causes eleven boiled oblations to be prepared, [in vessels] not made on a wheel.
[83].3) And two [vessels], one with a hundred holes and one with a thousand holes, a spade, salt earth, sand, a conch shell, water-lily root, powder made of all kinds of fragrant wood and of śamī wood, a boat made from a pacified tree, [and] a tripod.
[83].4) Two threads, a black one and a red one, unraveling, a left-twisted cord, four pegs from a pacified tree, four enclosing sticks: of vāraṇa, of śamī, of udumbara, and of palāśa wood; [and] pacified plants of the tree.
[83].5) He should deposit them in the month of Māgha, [saying,] 'Let there be no sin (mā-agha).'
[83].6) He should deposit them in autumn, [saying,] 'Let sin be pacified.'
[83].7) He should deposit them in summer, [saying,] 'Let sin be burned away.'
[83].8) He should deposit them on the new moon day, for the ancestors dwell at home [on that day].
[83].9) Now the resting-place [the burial ground]:
[83].10) That which is even, rooted with grass, unburnt, firm, and sloping toward the northeast;
[83].11) where trees and plants are free of thorns;
[83].12) and elevated, if he is one who desires heaven.
[83].13) Saying 'Tomorrow is the new moon day,' he procures a cow.
[83].14) Having deposited its left flank and cooked portion,
[83].15) he has alms collected.
[83].16) Having offered in the village the Yamasārasvata oblations,
[83].17) having walked around the resting-place with the two sprinkling waters with a branch of the kāmpīla tree,
[83].18) having cast down the branch toward the southeast, having ploughed [the ground] with a plough, [and] having enclosed it with branches,
[83].19) with 'Give back...' [AV 18.3.70], he takes [the bones] up from the foot of the tree.
[83].20) With 'What the black [bird has touched]...' [AV 18.3.55], having gathered [them] together from the earth onto a cloth, strewn [them] with powders of all fragrant substances, and raised [them] with raising verses, they should carry [them] with conveying verses,
[83].21) [or] dust from the place, if they do not find [the bones].
[83].22) Or, having spread a cloth at the water's edge, he should call, 'O so-and-so!'
[83].23) Whichever living creature alights there, having raised it with the raising verses, they should carry it with the conveying verses.
[83].24) Or three hundred and sixty palāśa-leaf stalks.
[83].25) In the village, he covers a shed having its doors to the south and north with darbha grass.
[83].26) The northern [door] is the passage for the living; the southern [door] is the passage for the ancestors.
[83].27) Before sunset, with 'Come hither...' [AV 18.4.62], he causes them to arrive.
[83].28) With 'Bending the knee...' [AV 18.1.52], he seats [them].
[83].29) With 'Let them enter together...' [AV 18.2.29], he causes them to lie down.
[83].30) With 'This is your vessel, O ancestors,' he pours out three cups of water.
[83].31) He causes three Brahmins who have bathed and anointed themselves to drink a mash of honey.
[83].32) He has the honey-mixture brought for the Brahman priest.
[83].33) They announce the cow.
[83].34) He says: 'Do it!'
[83].35) He feeds the right half of it to the Brahmins, [and offers] the left half to the ancestors.

83.s: śatātṛṇṇasahasrātṛṇṇau ca pāśīm ūṣam sikatāḥ śaṅkhaṃ śālūkaṃ sarvasurabhiśamīcūrṇakṛtaṃ śāntavṛkṣasya nāvaṃ tripādakam
83.d: शतातृण्णसहस्रातृण्णौ च पाशीम् ऊषम् सिकताः शङ्खं शालूकं सर्वसुरभिशमीचूर्णकृतं शान्तवृक्षस्य नावं त्रिपादकम्

83.s: dve niḥśīyamāne nīlalohite sūtre savyarajjuṃ śāntavṛkṣasya caturaḥ śaṅkūn caturaḥ paridhīn vāraṇaṃ śāmīlam audumbaraṃ pālāśaṃ vṛkṣasya śāntauṣadhīḥ
83.d: द्वे निःशीयमाने नीललोहिते सूत्रे सव्यरज्जुं शान्तवृक्षस्य चतुरः शङ्कून् चतुरः परिधीन् वारणं शामीलम् औदुम्बरं पालाशं वृक्षस्य शान्तौषधीः

83.s: amāvāsyāyāṃ nidadhyād amā hi pitaro bhavanti
83.d: अमावास्यायां निदध्याद् अमा हि पितरो भवन्ति

83.s: tad yat samaṃ samūlam avidagdhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ prāgudakpravaṇam
83.d: तद् यत् समं समूलम् अविदग्धं प्रतिष्ठितं प्रागुदक्प्रवणम्

83.s: tasyāḥ savyaṃ cāpaghanaṃ prapākaṃ ca nidhāya
83.d: तस्याः सव्यं चापघनं प्रपाकं च निधाय

83.s: prāgdakṣiṇaṃ śākhāṃ pravidhya sīreṇa karṣayitvā śākhābhiḥ parivārya
83.d: प्राग्दक्षिणं शाखां प्रविध्य सीरेण कर्षयित्वा शाखाभिः परिवार्य

83.s: yat te kṛṣṇaḥ iti bhūmer vasane samopya sarvasurabhicūrṇair avakīrya utthāpanībhir utthāpya hariṇībhir hareyuḥ
83.d: यत् ते कृष्णः इति भूमेर् वसने समोप्य सर्वसुरभिचूर्णैर् अवकीर्य उत्थापनीभिर् उत्थाप्य हरिणीभिर् हरेयुः

83.s: api vā udakānte vasanam āstīryāsau iti hvayet
83.d: अपि वा उदकान्ते वसनम् आस्तीर्यासौ इति ह्वयेत्

83.s: tatra yo jantur nipatet tam utthāpanībhir utthāpya hariṇībhir hareyuḥ
83.d: तत्र यो जन्तुर् निपतेत् तम् उत्थापनीभिर् उत्थाप्य हरिणीभिर् हरेयुः

83.s: etad vaḥ pitaraḥ pātram iti trīṇy udakaṃsān ninayati
83.d: एतद् वः पितरः पात्रम् इति त्रीण्य् उदकंसान् निनयति

83.s: tasyā dakṣiṇam ardhaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayati savyaṃ pitṝn
83.d: तस्या दक्षिणम् अर्धं ब्राह्मणान् भोजयति सव्यं पितॄन्

84.s: vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitān vettha nihitān parāke | medasaḥ kulyā upa tān sravantu satyā eṣām āśiṣaḥ santu kāmāḥ svāhā svadhā iti vapāyās trir juhoti
84.d: वह वपां जातवेदः पितृभ्यो यत्रैतान् वेत्थ निहितान् पराके । मेदसः कुल्या उप तान् स्रवन्तु सत्या एषाम् आशिषः सन्तु कामाः स्वाहा स्वधा इति वपायास् त्रिर् जुहोति
84.m:
[84].1) With 'Carry the omentum, O Jātavedas, to the ancestors, where you know them deposited far away; let streams of fat flow toward them, let their wishes be true, svāhā, svadhā!' he offers three times of the omentum.
[84].2) With 'This Yama...' [AV 18.1.60], [he offers] a fourth [oblation] to Yama.
[84].3) He cooks a kṛśara dish with twenty-one barley grains, and another mixed cooked dish.
[84].4) The living eat of that which is with barley.
[84].5) Then of the other he deposits a lump of food.
[84].6) With 'What mash [they have prepared] for you...' [AV 18.4.42], he deposits in the shed what is stated in the mantra.
[84].7) When its steam has risen, the servant-bearers eat it.
[84].8) He says: 'Let the lutes sound!'
[84].9) Saying, 'Exalt the ancestors!' having placed an empty jar in the middle of the shed, they beat it with an old shoe.
[84].10) With 'Wiping their tears...' [AV 18.3.17], with dishevelled hair, striking their right thighs, they go around counter-clockwise three times.
[84].11) Thus at midnight and in the latter part of the night.
[84].12) Before a marriage, there is a Piṇḍapitṛyajña with meat.
[84].13) Having raised [them] with the raising verses, they should carry [them] with the conveying verses.
[84].14) Then with 'Having settled...' [AV 18.4.44 / RV 10.169.1d], after the previously made [tombs], the earlier [rites] belong to the earlier ones, the later ones to the younger.
[84].15) Facing the southeast direction, they stand facing the northwest direction.
[84].16) As the funeral pyre is, so is the burial ground: sloping toward the southwest direction.

84.s: ekaviṃśatyā yavaiḥ kṛśaraṃ randhayati yutam anyat prapākaṃ ca
84.d: एकविंशत्या यवैः कृशरं रन्धयति युतम् अन्यत् प्रपाकं च

84.s: yaṃ te manthaṃ iti mantroktaṃ vimite nipṛṇāti
84.d: यं ते मन्थं इति मन्त्रोक्तं विमिते निपृणाति

84.s: mahayata pitṝn iti riktakumbhaṃ vimitamadhye nidhāya taṃ jaradupānahāghnanti
84.d: महयत पितॄन् इति रिक्तकुम्भं विमितमध्ये निधाय तं जरदुपानहाघ्नन्ति

84.s: kasye mṛjānā iti triḥ prasavyaṃ prakīrṇakeśyaḥ pariyanti dakṣiṇān ūrūn aghnānāḥ
84.d: कस्ये मृजाना इति त्रिः प्रसव्यं प्रकीर्णकेश्यः परियन्ति दक्षिणान् ऊरून् अघ्नानाः

84.s: atha avasāya iti paścāt pūrvakṛtebhyaḥ pūrvāṇi pūrvebhyo aparāṇi yavīyasām
84.d: अथ अवसाय इति पश्चात् पूर्वकृतेभ्यः पूर्वाणि पूर्वेभ्यो अपराणि यवीयसाम्

84.s: prāgdakṣiṇāṃ diśam abhy uttarām aparāṃ diśam abhitiṣṭhanti
84.d: प्राग्दक्षिणां दिशम् अभ्य् उत्तराम् अपरां दिशम् अभितिष्ठन्ति

84.s: yathā citiṃ tathā śmaśānaṃ dakṣiṇāparāṃ diśam abhi pravaṇam
84.d: यथा चितिं तथा श्मशानं दक्षिणापरां दिशम् अभि प्रवणम्

85.s: atha mānāni
85.d: अथ मानानि
85.m:
[85].1) Now the measurements:
[85].2) diṣṭi, kudiṣṭi, vitasti, nimuṣṭi, aratni, pada, and prakrama;
[85].3) with a prādeśa and with a bow, with [the mantra]: "We measure this measure" [AV 18.2.38].
[85].4) He measures seven on the south, seven on the north, five on the east, three on the west;
[85].5) or he measures nine on the south, nine on the north, seven on the east, five on the west;
[85].6) or he measures eleven on the south, eleven on the north, nine on the east, seven on the west;
[85].7) according to the Devadarśins, with eleven [units].
[85].8) According to the Śaunakins, [the enclosures] are of uneven measurements, circular or quadrangular;
[85].9) for so they are seen.
[85].10) As tall as a man with his arms raised, so high the fire-altar is piled.
[85].11) [The measures are] left-sided, having entrances on the south, with uneven numbers of stones and uneven numbers of bricks.
[85].12) Having measured off [the space] on the south with a left-twisted cord, with: "We measure this measure" [AV 18.2.38],
[85].13) with [the formula]: "May evil be warded off," he lays the vāraṇa enclosing-stick around and fastens the peg.
[85].14) Having measured on the east, with [the formula]: "May evil be pacified for them," he lays the śamī enclosing-stick around and fastens the peg.
[85].15) Having measured on the north, with [the formula]: "May evil be calmed," he lays the udumbara enclosing-stick around and fastens the peg.
[85].16) Having measured on the west, with [the formula]: "Evil is pacified," he lays the palāśa enclosing-stick around and fastens the peg.
[85].17) He consecrates [the area] with: "You are home" [AV 18.2.45].
[85].18) Having tied [it] crosswise with a red thread,
[85].19) having dug a pit in the middle with: "Praise the famous one" [AV 18.1.40], he scatters pāśi-stone, sand, saline earth, udumbara, conch-shell, lotus-root, all fragrant substances, and pulverized śamī-wood.
[85].20) With: "May evil fall away," he spreads out a fraying cloth.
[85].21) "Evil is not near."
[85].22) With: "May evil be torn apart," he tears apart a cloth of coarse wool around [it].
[85].23) The oblation and the strewing toward the south have [already] been stated.
[85].24) With: "Mount upon this" [AV 18.3.73] [and] "I give" [AV 18.2.37], the youngest [son] deposits [the bones].
[85].25) With: "Come to this barhis" [AV 18.4.52], the surviving son arranges [the bones] limb by limb.
[85].26) He consecrates them with the formulas beginning with: "Let not your mind..." [AV 18.2.24], "Whatever limb of yours..." [AV 18.2.26], "Indra... me..." [AV 18.3.25], up to: "The water-jars..." [AV 18.3.37].
[85].27) He scatters fried grains with the [verses] containing appropriate marks.

85.s: diṣṭikudiṣṭivitastinimuṣṭyaratnipadaprakramāḥ
85.d: दिष्टिकुदिष्टिवितस्तिनिमुष्ट्यरत्निपदप्रक्रमाः

85.s: prādeśena dhanuṣā ca imāṃ mātrāṃ mimīmahe iti
85.d: प्रादेशेन धनुषा च इमां मात्रां मिमीमहे इति

85.s: sapta dakṣiṇato mimīte sapta uttarataḥ pañca purastāt trīṇi paścāt
85.d: सप्त दक्षिणतो मिमीते सप्त उत्तरतः पञ्च पुरस्तात् त्रीणि पश्चात्

85.s: nava dakṣiṇato mimīte nava uttarataḥ sapta purastāt pañca paścāt
85.d: नव दक्षिणतो मिमीते नव उत्तरतः सप्त पुरस्तात् पञ्च पश्चात्

85.s: ekādaśa dakṣiṇato mimīta ekādaśa uttarato nava purastāt sapta paścāt
85.d: एकादश दक्षिणतो मिमीत एकादश उत्तरतो नव पुरस्तात् सप्त पश्चात्

85.s: ekādaśabhir devadarśinām
85.d: एकादशभिर् देवदर्शिनाम्

85.s: ayugmamānāni parimaṇḍalāni caturasrāṇi vā śaunakinām
85.d: अयुग्ममानानि परिमण्डलानि चतुरस्राणि वा शौनकिनाम्

85.s: tathā hi dṛśyante
85.d: तथा हि दृश्यन्ते

85.s: yāvān puruṣa ūrdhvanāhus tāvān agniś citaḥ
85.d: यावान् पुरुष ऊर्ध्वनाहुस् तावान् अग्निश् चितः

85.s: savyāni dakṣiṇādvārāṇi ayugmaśilāni ayugmeṣṭikāni ca
85.d: सव्यानि दक्षिणाद्वाराणि अयुग्मशिलानि अयुग्मेष्टिकानि च

85.s: imāṃ mātrāṃ mimīmahe iti dakṣiṇataḥ savyarajjuṃ mītvā
85.d: इमां मात्रां मिमीमहे इति दक्षिणतः सव्यरज्जुं मीत्वा

85.s: vārayatām agham iti vāraṇaṃ paridhiṃ paridadhāti śaṅkuṃ ca nicṛtati
85.d: वारयताम् अघम् इति वारणं परिधिं परिदधाति शङ्कुं च निचृतति

85.s: purastān mītvā śam ebhyo astv agham iti śāmīlaṃ paridhiṃ paridadhāti śaṅkuṃ ca nicṛtati
85.d: पुरस्तान् मीत्वा शम् एभ्यो अस्त्व् अघम् इति शामीलं परिधिं परिदधाति शङ्कुं च निचृतति

85.s: uttarato mītvā śāmyatv agham ity audumbaraṃ paridhiṃ paridadhāti śaṅkuṃ ca nicṛtati
85.d: उत्तरतो मीत्वा शाम्यत्व् अघम् इत्य् औदुम्बरं परिधिं परिदधाति शङ्कुं च निचृतति

85.s: paścān mītvā śāntam agham iti pālāśaṃ paridhiṃ paridadhāti śaṅkuṃ ca nicṛtati
85.d: पश्चान् मीत्वा शान्तम् अघम् इति पालाशं परिधिं परिदधाति शङ्कुं च निचृतति

85.s: amāsi ity anumantrayate
85.d: अमासि इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयते

85.s: akṣṇayā lohitasūtreṇa nibadhya
85.d: अक्ष्णया लोहितसूत्रेण निबध्य

85.s: stuhi śrutaṃ iti madhye gartaṃ khātvā pāśisikatā ūṣa udumbaraśaṅkhaśālūkasarvasurabhiśamīcūrṇāni nivapati
85.d: स्तुहि श्रुतं इति मध्ये गर्तं खात्वा पाशिसिकता ऊष उदुम्बरशङ्खशालूकसर्वसुरभिशमीचूर्णानि निवपति

85.s: niḥśīyatām agham iti niḥśīyamānam āstṛṇāti
85.d: निःशीयताम् अघम् इति निःशीयमानम् आस्तृणाति

85.s: asaṃpraty agham
85.d: असंप्रत्य् अघम्

85.s: vi lumpatām agham iti pari cailaṃ dūrśaṃ vilumpati
85.d: वि लुम्पताम् अघम् इति परि चैलं दूर्शं विलुम्पति

85.s: ukto homo dakṣiṇata staraṇaṃ ca
85.d: उक्तो होमो दक्षिणत स्तरणं च

85.s: etad ā roha dadāmi iti kaniṣṭho nivapati
85.d: एतद् आ रोह ददामि इति कनिष्ठो निवपति

85.s: edaṃ barhir iti sthitasūnur yathāparu saṃcinoti
85.d: एदं बर्हिर् इति स्थितसूनुर् यथापरु संचिनोति

85.s: mā te mano yat te aṅgam indro mā udapūr ity āto anumantrayate
85.d: मा ते मनो यत् ते अङ्गम् इन्द्रो मा उदपूर् इत्य् आतो अनुमन्त्रयते

85.s: dhānāḥ saliṅgābhir āvapati
85.d: धानाः सलिङ्गाभिर् आवपति

86.s: idaṃ kasāmbu iti sajātān avekṣayati
86.d: इदं कसाम्बु इति सजातान् अवेक्षयति
86.m:
[86].1) With: "This is kasāmbu" [AV 18.4.37], he has the kinsmen look.
[86].2) Having filled the boiled oblation with clarified butter and honey, he places it at the region of the head with: "And those who are alive..." [AV 18.4.57] [and] "Those your ancestors who have departed..." [AV 18.3.72].
[86].3) With: "Possessing cakes..." [AV 18.4.16], he places what is mentioned in the mantra in the directions and in the eighth regions.
[86].4) In the middle, the cooking-vessel.
[86].5) Having poured water over it with: "A thousand-streamed, a hundred-streamed..." [AV 18.4.36],
[86].6) he covers it with middle palāśa leaves with: "The parṇa-tree is king..." [AV 18.4.53];
[86].7) with stones with: "The share of strength..." [AV 18.4.54];
[86].8) [and] with clods of earth limb by limb with: "I prop you up..." [AV 18.3.52].
[86].9) Having covered it with a fraying cloth with: "May evil fall away," and having strewn it with darbha grass,
[86].10) they pile [the mound] with: "This indeed is ours..." [AV 18.2.50], "Crawl near..." [AV 18.3.49], [and] "Yonder indeed..." [AV 18.4.66].
[86].11) Having leaned [against it] with: "As for Yama..." [AV 18.4.55],
[86].12) with: "May evil be broken," he places a bunch [of grass] above the head.
[86].13) According to some, [this is] forbidden.
[86].14) With: "Evil is hidden," he erects an eight-finger-long reed-bundle of non-spotted stalks toward the direction of the village.
[86].15) Having sprinkled water counter-clockwise, they break the water-jars.
[86].16) With: "Assemble..." [AV 7.21.1], they take hold of fixed [wooden sticks] at the western corner of the burial ground.
[86].17) To the west and north of the fire, [the recitation continues] from: "With splendor me..." [AV 18.3.10], "Vivasvant..." [AV 18.3.61], [and] "Indra, the resolve..." [AV 18.3.67].
[86].18) With: "They kindle together..." [AV 18.4.41], he kindles the saṃkasuka fire behind.
[86].19) With: "In this we..." [AV 12.2.13], "Whatever defilement..." [AV 12.2.40], [and] "Wipe yourselves on lead..." [AV 12.2.19], he causes them to wash their limbs.
[86].20) Having wiped their hands and feet with black wool,
[86].21) [they do] what is mentioned in the mantras with: "These living ones..." [AV 12.2.22] [and] "With upward-turned..." [AV 12.2.29].
[86].22) Having effaced the footprints from the burial ground with a kūdī twig with: "Thrice seven..." [AV 12.2.29c],
[86].23) [and] with the second [hemistich]: "Death's footprint..." [AV 12.2.30], [those] of the boats,
[86].24) [and] having thrown the kūdī twig toward the southeast with: "Far away, O Death..." [AV 12.2.21],
[86].25) having caused seven mock rivers to be made and having filled them with water,
[86].26) with: "Mount this boat of Savitṛ..." [AV 12.2.48c], "Good guardian..." [AV 7.6.3], [and] "Great indeed..." [AV 7.6.2], he makes them mount a boat containing gold and barley.
[86].27) With: "The stony [river] flows..." [AV 12.2.26] [and] "Rise up, cross over, companions..." [AV 12.2.27], he makes them cross toward the north.
[86].28) From the pebble [ritual] up to the placing of the kindling stick [is as previously described].
[86].29) The [rites] beginning with the formula to Vaivasvata are identical.
[86].30) Having reached home, the ancestral offering with rice balls is the same.

86.s: ye ca jīvā ye te pūrve parāgatā iti sarpirmadhubhyāṃ caruṃ pūrayitvā śīrṣadeśe nidadhāti
86.d: ये च जीवा ये ते पूर्वे परागता इति सर्पिर्मधुभ्यां चरुं पूरयित्वा शीर्षदेशे निदधाति

86.s: apūpavān iti mantroktaṃ dikṣu aṣṭamadeśeṣu nidadhāti
86.d: अपूपवान् इति मन्त्रोक्तं दिक्षु अष्टमदेशेषु निदधाति

86.s: madhye pacantam
86.d: मध्ये पचन्तम्

86.s: sahasradhāraṃ śatadhāram ity adbhir abhiviṣyandya
86.d: सहस्रधारं शतधारम् इत्य् अद्भिर् अभिविष्यन्द्य

86.s: parṇo rājā iti madhyamapalāśair abhinidadhāti
86.d: पर्णो राजा इति मध्यमपलाशैर् अभिनिदधाति

86.s: ūrjo bhāgo ity aśmabhiḥ
86.d: ऊर्जो भागो इत्य् अश्मभिः

86.s: ut te stabhnāmi iti logān yathāparu
86.d: उत् ते स्तभ्नामि इति लोगान् यथापरु

86.s: niḥśīyatām agham iti niḥśīyamānenāvachādya darbhair avastīrya
86.d: निःशीयताम् अघम् इति निःशीयमानेनावछाद्य दर्भैर् अवस्तीर्य

86.s: idam id vā u na upa sarpa asau hā iti cinvanti
86.d: इदम् इद् वा उ न उप सर्प असौ हा इति चिन्वन्ति

86.s: yathā yamāya iti saṃśritya
86.d: यथा यमाय इति संश्रित्य

86.s: śṛṇātv agham ity upariśira stambam ādadhāti
86.d: शृणात्व् अघम् इत्य् उपरिशिर स्तम्बम् आदधाति

86.s: pratiṣiddham ekeṣām
86.d: प्रतिषिद्धम् एकेषाम्

86.s: akalmāṣāṇāṃ kāṇḍānām aṣṭāṅgulīṃ tejanīm antarhitam agham iti grāmadeśād ucchrayati
86.d: अकल्माषाणां काण्डानाम् अष्टाङ्गुलीं तेजनीम् अन्तर्हितम् अघम् इति ग्रामदेशाद् उच्छ्रयति

86.s: prasavyaṃ pariṣicya kumbhān bhindanti
86.d: प्रसव्यं परिषिच्य कुम्भान् भिन्दन्ति

86.s: sameta iti aparasyāṃ śmaśānasraktyāṃ dhruvanāni upayachante
86.d: समेत इति अपरस्यां श्मशानस्रक्त्यां ध्रुवनानि उपयछन्ते

86.s: paścād uttarato agner varcasā māṃ vivasvān indra kratuṃ ity ātaḥ
86.d: पश्चाद् उत्तरतो अग्नेर् वर्चसा मां विवस्वान् इन्द्र क्रतुं इत्य् आतः

86.s: sam indhate iti paścāt saṃkasukam uddīpayati
86.d: सम् इन्धते इति पश्चात् संकसुकम् उद्दीपयति

86.s: asmin vayaṃ yad ripraṃ sīse mṛḍḍhvaṃ ity abhyavanejayati
86.d: अस्मिन् वयं यद् रिप्रं सीसे मृड्ढ्वं इत्य् अभ्यवनेजयति

86.s: kṛṣṇorṇayā pāṇipādān nimṛjya
86.d: कृष्णोर्णया पाणिपादान् निमृज्य

86.s: ime jīvā udīcīnaiḥ iti mantroktam
86.d: इमे जीवा उदीचीनैः इति मन्त्रोक्तम्

86.s: triḥ sapta iti kūdyā padāni lopayitvā śmaśānāt
86.d: त्रिः सप्त इति कूद्या पदानि लोपयित्वा श्मशानात्

86.s: mṛtyoḥ padaṃ iti dvitīyayā nāvaḥ
86.d: मृत्योः पदं इति द्वितीयया नावः

86.s: paraṃ mṛtyo iti prāgdakṣiṇam kūdīṃ pravidhya
86.d: परं मृत्यो इति प्राग्दक्षिणम् कूदीं प्रविध्य

86.s: sapta nadīrūpāṇi kārayitvā udakena pūrayitvā
86.d: सप्त नदीरूपाणि कारयित्वा उदकेन पूरयित्वा

86.s: ā rohata savitur nāvam etāṃ sutrāmāṇaṃ mahīm ū ṣu iti sahiraṇyāṃ sayavāṃ nāvam ārohayati
86.d: आ रोहत सवितुर् नावम् एतां सुत्रामाणं महीम् ऊ षु इति सहिरण्यां सयवां नावम् आरोहयति

86.s: aśmanvatī rīyate ut tiṣṭhatā pra taratā sakhāyo ity udīcas tārayati
86.d: अश्मन्वती रीयते उत् तिष्ठता प्र तरता सखायो इत्य् उदीचस् तारयति

86.s: śarkarādi ā samidādhānāt
86.d: शर्करादि आ समिदाधानात्

86.s: vaivasvatādi samānam
86.d: वैवस्वतादि समानम्

86.s: prāpya gṛhān samānaḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñaḥ
86.d: प्राप्य गृहान् समानः पिण्डपितृयज्ञः

87.s: atha piṇḍapitṛyajñaḥ
87.d: अथ पिण्डपितृयज्ञः
87.m:
[87].1) Now, the offering of rice-balls to the ancestors.
[87].2) It is understood [to be performed] on the new moon day, in the evening, when the day declines.
[87].3) With "May Mitra and Varuṇa wrap around me [18.3.12]", he washes both hands.
[87].4) With "Me with splendor [18.3.10]", he sips water.
[87].5) Having sipped water with the left [hand], shifting [the cord] to the right, he instructs the order-carrier:
[87].6) "Wash the mortar and pestle, the winnowing basket, the boiled oblation [pot], [and] the bronze bowl; bring the sacrificial grass and the water jar."
[87].7) Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, facing the intermediate southeast direction, he pours out into the winnowing basket the sacrificial oblation substances, separated by a single strainer.
[87].8) He pours out three [portions] downward-pointing, [saying]: "This for Agni the bearer of funeral offerings [18.4.71], svadhā to the ancestors sitting upon the earth [18.4.78]"; "This for Soma possessed of ancestors, svadhā [18.4.72], to the ancestors accompanied by Soma [18.4.73], or to the ancestors sitting in intermediate space [18.4.79]"; "This for Yama possessed of ancestors [18.4.74], and svadhā to the ancestors sitting in heaven [18.4.80]".
[87].9) Throwing [them] into the mortar, he pounds three times, [saying]: "This is your sacrificial oblation, O ancestors!"
[87].10) As [with] a sacrificial oblation, so he attends [to it].
[87].11) For the sacrifice to the ancestors is indeed a sacrificial oblation.
[87].12) They instruct the order-carrier: "Wash the boiled oblation [pot], place it on the fire, pour in water, throw in the hulled grains; do not sit stirring with the stirring stick; do not hold [your] head."
[87].13) They censure holding the head.
[87].14) Having gone outside, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, facing the intermediate southeast direction, he digs a furrow of a span's measure, an finger's breadth across, with "Let them arise [18.1.44]".
[87].15) A finger's breadth downward and a joint's measure, say some.
[87].16) With "Struck down are the Asuras, the Rakṣases, who sit among the ancestors", he scrapes up the loose earth toward the southeast.
[87].17) Having washed both the furrow and his hands, having filled the furrow with water with "This is your vessel, O ancestors",
[87].18) having passed inside, having seasoned [the caru] with sour milk or fresh butter, having moved it out toward the south,
[87].19) having taken two pieces of wood, he kindles [them] with "Desiring [18.1.56]".
[87].20) Of the two kindled, he puts back one.
[87].21) Taking one with "Remain right here, winning wealth [18.4.38]",
[87].22) having placed it on the loose earth, he adds fuel with "Those who are buried [18.2.34]", "They kindle together [18.4.41]", "Those who thirsted [18.3.47]", [and] "Those who are true [18.3.48]".
[87].23) He sets down the ritual equipment.
[87].24) The sprinkling vessel, the sacrificial grass, the water jar, the bronze bowl, the wooden ladle, the ghee, the stirring ladle, the boiled oblation, garments, eye-salve, [and] ointment.
[87].25) Whatever is to be brought together here, having brought that together,
[87].26) then, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder [and then] wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, having taken the sacrificial grass, having untied the binding, he should throw [it] down toward the southwestern eighth region.
[87].27) Having besprinkled the sacrificial grass with water, he spreads it out with "O ancestors who sit on the sacrificial grass [18.1.51]", "Invited are our ancestors [18.3.45]", "The ancestors consumed by Agni [18.3.44]", "Those who are the ancestors of our father [18.3.46]", [and] "Those of us [18.4.68]".
[87].28) Three [offerings/vessels] beginning with the stirring ladle.
[87].29) With the three [verses] "Let them arise [18.1.44]", he should pour out the water vessels verse by verse.
[87].30) Then, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder [and then] wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, with "Those who are Dasyus [18.2.28]", having moved a firebrand lit at both ends three times counter-clockwise, he casts [it] away.
[87].31) Having sprinkled around,

87.s: amāvāsyāyāṃ sāyaṃ nyahne ahani vijñāyate
87.d: अमावास्यायां सायं न्यह्ने अहनि विज्ञायते

87.s: mitrāvaruṇā pari mām adhātām iti pāṇī prakṣālayate
87.d: मित्रावरुणा परि माम् अधाताम् इति पाणी प्रक्षालयते

87.s: varcasā māṃ ity ācāmati
87.d: वर्चसा मां इत्य् आचामति

87.s: punaḥ savyenācamanād apasavyaṃ kṛtvā praiṣakṛtaṃ samādiśati
87.d: पुनः सव्येनाचमनाद् अपसव्यं कृत्वा प्रैषकृतं समादिशति

87.s: ulūkhalamusalaṃ śūrpaṃ caruṃ kaṃsaṃ prakṣālaya barhir udakumbham ā hara iti
87.d: उलूखलमुसलं शूर्पं चरुं कंसं प्रक्षालय बर्हिर् उदकुम्भम् आ हर इति

87.s: yajñopavītī dakṣiṇapūrvam antardeśam abhimukhaḥ śūrpa ekapavitrāntarhitān haviṣyān nirvapati
87.d: यज्ञोपवीती दक्षिणपूर्वम् अन्तर्देशम् अभिमुखः शूर्प एकपवित्रान्तर्हितान् हविष्यान् निर्वपति

87.s: idam agnaye kavyavāhanāya svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ pṛthiviṣadbhyaḥ itīdaṃ somāya pitṛmate svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ somavadbhyaḥ pitṛbhyo vāntarikṣasadbhyaḥ itīdaṃ yamāya pitṛmate svadhā pitṛbhyaś ca diviṣadbhyaḥ iti trīn avācīnakāśīn nirvapati
87.d: इदम् अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय स्वधा पितृभ्यः पृथिविषद्भ्यः इतीदं सोमाय पितृमते स्वधा पितृभ्यः सोमवद्भ्यः पितृभ्यो वान्तरिक्षसद्भ्यः इतीदं यमाय पितृमते स्वधा पितृभ्यश् च दिविषद्भ्यः इति त्रीन् अवाचीनकाशीन् निर्वपति

87.s: ulūkhala opya trir avahanti idaṃ vaḥ pitaro haviḥ iti
87.d: उलूखल ओप्य त्रिर् अवहन्ति इदं वः पितरो हविः इति

87.s: yathā havis tathā paricarati
87.d: यथा हविस् तथा परिचरति

87.s: havir hi eva pitṛyajñaḥ
87.d: हविर् हि एव पितृयज्ञः

87.s: praiṣakṛtaṃ samādiśanti caruṃ prakṣālayādhiśrayāpa opya taṇḍulān āvapasva nekṣaṇena yodhayann āsva mā śiro grahīḥ
87.d: प्रैषकृतं समादिशन्ति चरुं प्रक्षालयाधिश्रयाप ओप्य तण्डुलान् आवपस्व नेक्षणेन योधयन्न् आस्व मा शिरो ग्रहीः

87.s: śirograhaṃ paricakṣate
87.d: शिरोग्रहं परिचक्षते

87.s: bāhyena upaniṣkramya yajñopavītī dakṣiṇapūrvam antardeśam abhimukha ud īratām iti karṣūṃ khanati prādeśamātrīṃ tiryagaṅgurim
87.d: बाह्येन उपनिष्क्रम्य यज्ञोपवीती दक्षिणपूर्वम् अन्तर्देशम् अभिमुख उद् ईरताम् इति कर्षूं खनति प्रादेशमात्रीं तिर्यगङ्गुरिम्

87.s: avāgaṅguriṃ parvamātrīm ity eke
87.d: अवागङ्गुरिं पर्वमात्रीम् इत्य् एके

87.s: apahatā asurā rakṣāṃsi ye pitṛṣadaḥ iti prāgdakṣiṇaṃ pāṃsūn udūhati
87.d: अपहता असुरा रक्षांसि ये पितृषदः इति प्राग्दक्षिणं पांसून् उदूहति

87.s: karṣūṃ ca pāṇī ca prakṣālya etad vaḥ pitaraḥ pātram iti karṣūm udakena pūrayitvā
87.d: कर्षूं च पाणी च प्रक्षाल्य एतद् वः पितरः पात्रम् इति कर्षूम् उदकेन पूरयित्वा

87.s: antarupātītya mastunā navanītena vā pratinīya dakṣiṇāñcam udvāsya
87.d: अन्तरुपातीत्य मस्तुना नवनीतेन वा प्रतिनीय दक्षिणाञ्चम् उद्वास्य

87.s: dve kāṣṭhe gṛhītvā uśantas ity ādīpayati
87.d: द्वे काष्ठे गृहीत्वा उशन्तस् इत्य् आदीपयति

87.s: ādīptayor ekaṃ pratinidadhāti
87.d: आदीप्तयोर् एकं प्रतिनिदधाति

87.s: ihaivaidhi dhanasanir ity ekaṃ hṛtvā
87.d: इहैवैधि धनसनिर् इत्य् एकं हृत्वा

87.s: pāṃsuṣu ādhāya upasamādadhāti ye nikhātāḥ sam indhate ye tātṛṣur ye satyāso iti
87.d: पांसुषु आधाय उपसमादधाति ये निखाताः सम् इन्धते ये तातृषुर् ये सत्यासो इति

87.s: saṃbhārān upasādayati
87.d: संभारान् उपसादयति

87.s: paryukṣaṇīṃ barhir udakumbhaṃ kaṃsaṃ darvim ājyam āyavanaṃ caruṃ vāsāṃsy āñjanam abhyañjanam iti
87.d: पर्युक्षणीं बर्हिर् उदकुम्भं कंसं दर्विम् आज्यम् आयवनं चरुं वासांस्य् आञ्जनम् अभ्यञ्जनम् इति

87.s: yad atra upasamāhāryaṃ bhavati tad upasamāhṛtya
87.d: यद् अत्र उपसमाहार्यं भवति तद् उपसमाहृत्य

87.s: ato yajñopavītī pitryupavītī barhir gṛhītvā vicṛtya saṃnahanaṃ dakṣiṇāparam aṣṭamadeśam abhyavāsyet
87.d: अतो यज्ञोपवीती पित्र्युपवीती बर्हिर् गृहीत्वा विचृत्य संनहनं दक्षिणापरम् अष्टमदेशम् अभ्यवास्येत्

87.s: barhir udakena saṃprokṣya barhiṣadaḥ pitara upahūtā naḥ pitaraḥ agniṣvāttāḥ pitaro ye naḥ pituḥ pitaro ye 'smākaṃ iti prastṛṇāti
87.d: बर्हिर् उदकेन संप्रोक्ष्य बर्हिषदः पितर उपहूता नः पितरः अग्निष्वात्ताः पितरो ये नः पितुः पितरो ये ऽस्माकं इति प्रस्तृणाति

87.s: āyāpanādīni trīṇi
87.d: आयापनादीनि त्रीणि

87.s: ud īratām iti tisṛbhir udapātrāṇi anvṛcaṃ ninayet
87.d: उद् ईरताम् इति तिसृभिर् उदपात्राणि अन्वृचं निनयेत्

87.s: ataḥ pitryupavītī yajñopavītī ye dasyavaḥ ity ubhayata ādīptam ulmukaṃ triḥ prasavyaṃ parihṛtya nirasyati
87.d: अतः पित्र्युपवीती यज्ञोपवीती ये दस्यवः इत्य् उभयत आदीप्तम् उल्मुकं त्रिः प्रसव्यं परिहृत्य निरस्यति

87.s: paryukṣya
87.d: पर्युक्ष्य
